googleReviews.author: Abby Weeden
googleReviews.text:
We booked a private karaoke room for our group of seven and had the time of our lives singing our little hearts out for three hours. Their karaoke system using the tv, mics, and provided tablet all worked great. And when we had a brief moment of connectivity issues with our mic, they quickly fixed it and we were back to scream singing 90's country songs in mere moments.

They had a service button in our room for when we needed to request items from the bar. This button only seemed to work like half of the time, so we would try and order for the group all at once and getting buckets. The couple of times we tried to order anything but the buckets of beer, the orders were slightly wrong and a couple of us never got our drinks but it took so long to get any assistance that we just gave up.

The private rooms are literally in the basement of the diviest dive karaoke bar. Which didn't bother us at all, just know what to expect.

googleReviews.author: william nunez del rio
googleReviews.text: I’m not picky at all, but our experience at this place was terrible. Even though we were paying customers, we were treated in a clearly discriminatory way, were kicked out of the karaoke, and the staff was extremely rude. On top of that, we were given a misleading offer and ended up being charged more than promised. I do not recommend this place at all. It’s much better to go to Koreatown, where the vibe is cooler and the people are genuinely friendly.

googleReviews.author: Maria
googleReviews.text:
Came to try this spot out last night because I'd heard great things. The vibe, atmosphere, and overall setup were cool, but unfortunately they seemed too crowded and understaffed. We were in a room and were told to press the service button on the wall when we needed assistance, but it often took quite a while for someone to come over. Because of that, we ended up having to walk to the already crowded bar multiple times just to order drinks.

It wasn't the most pleasant experience and definitely took away from the night. What made it more disappointing is that other karaoke spots in the neighborhood and Koreatown generally provide much better service, even when they're busy on weekends. Hopefully they can improve staffing and crowd management during busy hours. I'd be willing to give it another shot on a slower night, but I probably wouldn't return on a packed weekend based on this experience.

googleReviews.author: Alex G
googleReviews.text: The best karaoke bar in the city !!! First off the security guard Wayne is extremely professional but also personable and supportive to all guests. Come here for Leo , Kevin, or Mark bartending! always bringing the best vibes. You can get a private room or just sing and drink at the bar. It’s always open until 4am which is a plus for a night owl like myself. People who rate this place 1 star must not go out often.

googleReviews.author: Micah Wolfe
googleReviews.text: Sing Sing is my spot! I absolutely love going there. Leo is the best. A great and attentive bartender who brings the vibes. Kevin is also fire. AND WADE! Security. He sings with guest and always makes me feel welcome. I highly recommend karaoke-ing over there whenever you get the chance!

googleReviews.text:
Where can I start? One of the most fun, inclusive bars in Syracuse. Excellent attentive staff that makes you feel welcomed and want to ensure you have a fun time. I've been coming here almost 15 years, and whether I was gone for a week, a month, or a year, I always felt like I never left. An enormous library of songs to choose from.

Worried about singing terribly? No worries! People will still clap and cheer no matter what you sing or how off key. It about having fun.

This place is magic. If you're new here, you're sure to make a friend or several before you leave for the night.

googleReviews.author: elongatedpsudonym
googleReviews.text: This place banged, no notes. Not even several feet of snow could keep this place from being an absolute vibe on a saturday night. Even the simple bar food was fresh and competently prepared. Worth mutliple hours of driving, just for the ideal karaoke bar experience. If you run a karaoke bar, or plan to, take notes. This is how you do it.

googleReviews.author: Alexandria Ayala
googleReviews.text: There was good food, nice staff, and people. Don't be afraid to get up there and sing, no one is judgemental! Everyone will cheer you on, and even dance and sing with you 😎

googleReviews.author: Mia Quatrone
googleReviews.text: Feels like home. Always a safe and welcoming place to go. I’m almost 4 years sober and am very comfortable going and enjoying myself. I love the people, love the singing, competing in Superstar Syracuse and doing comedy at the occasional open mic. Holly even made sure to move extra watermelon Redbull upstairs one day when I didn’t enjoy the other flavor (other than regular or sugar free regular), because I’m sober and she knows that’s what my sober drink is!

googleReviews.author: A. McCullough
googleReviews.text: This is a great place to hangout with a group of friends!  The Karaoke is free, but you have to wait your turn.  People can perform on stage with props, or sing from the bar.  The food and drinks are reasonably priced, but the drinks are watered down.  We had several rounds of shots and mixed drinks and none of us were wasted (no hangovers either).   People have to go to the bar to order food and drinks. The straws are not covered, and the waitresses put them into people's drinks with their bare hands, which isn't very sanitary, but no one seemed to mind (that would NOT fly where I live).   To sing, people write their name and song request on a slip of paper and give it to the DJ.  I believe the regulars know to get their song requests in early because the same people performed multiple times.  This spot is a small bar with limited seating, so arrive early to get a table or a seat.  The pool table is in the bar area. The crowd was mixed and everyone was friendly and supportive!  I definitely would do it again.

googleReviews.author: Brenda Martinez
googleReviews.text: I went to Happy Karaoke to celebrate my son's 13th birthday today. After doing a lot of research I chose them because of the great reviews. What can I say? They did not disappoint  I made my reservation with Daniel (the manager) two weeks ago and he was great. He explained everything to me. I booked a room for 6 kids and 6 adults. Since we were the chaperones with the kids. Daniel was an amazing host. Explained to us how to use the karoake machine and equipment. They had lots of props, like maracas, tambourine, hats, bright frilly jackets, glasses. The room we had was big and comfortable with plenty of room and seating and a coat rack. We ordered beverages from the place. We were allowed to get pizza delivered and bring our own cake. They provided complimentary popcorn that was a nice touch. I loved the setup. My girlfriend's and I are already setting up a ladies day out to do karaoke in April. Place was spotless including the bathrooms. The whole place was great. Parking is a challenge but we found parking a block away in a residential area. If you are looking for a fun, clean and affordable karoake place do not look any further... Happy Karaoke is your place!! Thank you again! See you in April!!

googleReviews.author: Sherry V
googleReviews.text:
We had a fantastic family night out at this karaoke place! Our group of 6, including 3 teens, 2 adults, and a 3-year-old who amazed us by knowing the words to 'Let It Go.’  We arrived at 6 pm on a Saturday night. Parking was convenient with street parking paid until 8:30 pm. The location had a few steps to walk down, but it was worth it.

The friendly receptionist explained the remote that was mainly in Korean but the color-coded system and some English song titles made it easy to use. Despite the language difference, it was a breeze. The clean room came with 2 mics, each with protective covers. We quickly mastered the remote, so we didn't need assistance.

We didn't order food or drinks, but the overall experience was a blast. After two hours of singing, we were ready to eat and headed to a nearby Korean BBQ restaurant. It was a fun-filled night for the whole family!

googleReviews.author: shirley avelar
googleReviews.text: Yesterday my friends and I made a reservation at this location for 9:00pm. It was 8 of us so we called a day before to make the reservation for two hours. When we made the reservation we were told it was $15 per person, we even asked how much would it be including the fees and tip. When my friends and I arrived we were early, we didn’t want to enter the room just in case they would charge us off the bat. we asked the guy working there how much is the gratuity he stated it was 20% now let’s keep this in mind. When the rest of my group came our timer immediately started, we were there for two hours having fun- celebrating my friend’s birthday. when we see our two hours is up I decided to ask for the bill, which is should’ve been around $280-300 for the amount of time we were there and the two bottles of soju we ordered. Come to my surprise it was $523, which karaoke should NOT be that high not even in the city would they charge that much. My friend asked how much was the gratuity and he said it was 30%… which threw me off because in the beginning he said it was 20% so why did he change it to 30%?? Then he told us that we never confirmed the reservation for two hours. My question is why would I have to confirm a reservation if no changes were made?? I understand we need to call if there’s any changes to said reservation but it stayed the same, so why should I have to call to confirm?? This isn’t the first time this has happened unfortunately. For my birthday I went here to celebrate as well and the bill was ridiculously high and it was mostly in the hidden fees and the tip. Which again I paid it full price that time because I didn’t want to cause any issues, but this time it was ridiculous… an extra $200 was added with no explanation, no reason as to why the tip was extremely high, and mind you not once did he check up on us, the fan was broken and the ac wasn’t working. My issue besides the extra $200 that was charged how did $15 per person go to $51 per person. Would never come back again and wouldn’t recommend this place unless you want to pay for an overpriced karaoke experience lol.

googleReviews.author: Ben
googleReviews.text: Came here with friends and honestly had such a good time. The rooms were clean, the sound system was solid. Luke & Jessie was nice and checked in on us, which I appreciated. Great spot on Northern Blvd if you’re just trying to sing your heart out and have fun. Would definitely come back.

googleReviews.author: Nicholas Miller
googleReviews.text: Great experience hosting a birthday party here for 30+ people. The party room was spacious and clean upon arrival (pics below). Luke and Jessie were a pleasure to work with and we appreciate the accomodations that they gave to us because we were a larger group. Be warned that the room rental and any drink orders are subject to an automatic "20% gratuity," which sometimes works out be an even higher percentage by the way they calculate it (which adds a considerable amount to the bills).

googleReviews.author: SCOUR
googleReviews.text: This place was perfect for a party. The cocktails were actually really good (not watered down), and the sound system was amazing. We booked a room for a group and had an amazing time singing, drinking, and just hanging out. The staffs was amazing as well and the whole night went smoothly. Great spot on Northern Blvd if you’re celebrating something or just want a fun night out with friends.

googleReviews.author: Kenny Bello
googleReviews.text: Last night, we had an amazing time at Singing Karaoke. Luke and the staff went above and beyond to ensure we had an awesome celebration for our friend's 30th birthday. The entrance to the venue was bright and stylish, and the rooms were spacious and clean, which we really appreciated. There were endless song options to choose from. The cost is $15 per person per hour. We were given complimentary popcorn as well as menus to order food and drinks. While the place is not BYOB, you can bring outside food for an additional charge. The bathroom was also very clean. Overall, we all had a great time and highly recommend this place. Thank you Luke and staff!

googleReviews.author: K C
googleReviews.text:
I came here for my birthday and I highly recommend this place. The staff was great at making sure we were all taken care of while enjoying karaoke. It was a pleasure celebrating with my friends and family in a private room where we could sing our hearts out without any issues.
We did the BYOB package, which was a fair price at $51 per person for a group of 11. I recommend contacting them in advance to let them know if you’re running late or if anything changes—especially when planning with a large group, as things can come up.
Thank you all for being so great and for making my 30th birthday celebration special!

googleReviews.author: Rudy Lee
googleReviews.text:
The customer service here was pretty hostile upon arrival, average exchanges with the entry staff and bartender always had a hint of attitude. I read some previous reviews stating that they will bring out a birthday cake if requested, so I bought a cake and made the request; the host could have simply declined but he was extremely passive aggressive in doing so for some reason. I ended up plating the cake myself in the room, which is fine.

We had to wait for our room to open and was directed to the bar. I got a drink and asked how much it was, in which the bar tender, Hanna, still didn’t tell me after serving it and instead asked if I wanted to close my tab. Once closing my tab, she charged my card for the drink AND karaoke room package. The small, watered down, drink was $19, and not until after charging me did she say gratuity for everything was already included. I’m not one to complain about automatic gratuity, but an $80 tip for some of the rudest customer service BEFORE we had even begun is asinine.

The karaoke room was fun, but the entry service left a bad taste in my mouth. Additionally, we were asked if we wanted to extend our time, but were told we would have to purchase one drink per person. This didn’t make sense considering we bought the drink package and still had a considerable amount of our drinks left. I would not recommend this place due to the service, and if you do decide to go, make sure you have a large group. The price tag is hefty, especially with taxes and automatic gratuity included.

googleReviews.author: Jasmine Johnson
googleReviews.text:
My family had a great time at Space Karaoke! We came in not too long after they opened. Our karaoke room looked amazing and the room was clean. The staff was kind and professional. I already did research before arriving about prices, but I still appreciate that they were upfront about their pricing and their policies before we paid for the room. I like that through Youtube we had a wide selection of songs for us to choose.

The only reason I didn’t give it 5 stars is because I wish we could’ve booked the room for longer than 1 hour without having to buy a party package. Booking the room for 2 hours or longer requires a package to be purchased. Otherwise, we had a great time.

googleReviews.author: Ariel Valentin
googleReviews.text:
Had a blast with my team for a work outing.

Don’t try any food so I can’t speak to the quality.

The sound system and mics were great.

The YouTube queuing playlist was a little confusing it was difficult to remove or adjust the queue but the good thing is it made it did make it easy for us to look up pretty much any song we wanted to sing.

The room for very hot with more than 6 people so dress comfortably if you rent a room and have a group lever than that.

googleReviews.text: One of my favorite places to go out with friends. Highly recommend. Great place and phenomenal vibes.

googleReviews.text: We came for a birthday 🎂 celebration and Justin was awesome!  Great catalog and great experience.  We opted for a private room and Justin was super friendly and accommodating.  I would come back .  The cocktails 🍹 were also great

googleReviews.author: Dee Mandiyan
googleReviews.text:
Had a great time in our room at Karaoke City. We had a pretty large group and Joon was diligent about charging us based on how many folks were there for how long, which I thought was really nice. Staff were really attentive and quick to respond to calls from us, and went over the equipment a few times to make sure everyone who arrived at different times knew how to work things. I appreciated their kindness.

After our time in our room was over, we went to the general bar. Service there was pretty speedy and it was spacious. Sadly, the space was quickly taken over by xenophobic frat boys, so we left. Not blaming staff at all for that--it was clearly not a good experience for them either--just naming a possibility that visitors might want to prepare for.

googleReviews.author: Bets
googleReviews.text: this is my second time coming here and it’s so fun! everything is clean and they have a great selection of music. friends and I had so much fun

googleReviews.author: Shayla Pachucho
googleReviews.text: The staff was extremely helpful and answered every question we had. They were open during the daytime, and our room was ready as soon as we arrived. The rooms are very private, and we couldn’t hear any noise from others. They provided an iPad for song selection, but we could also use our own phones to add songs to the queue. The microphones sounded great, and the audio was clear with easy control over the volume and sound settings. There was a huge variety of music choices, including rap, pop, country, and even some Mexican songs. They also served both Korean and American appetizers. The employee helping us was very attentive and made sure we were taken care of the whole time.

googleReviews.author: Foodiemesh
googleReviews.text:
1. We had a reservation for 10 but didn't get into our rooms until 10:30. They had clearly overbooked the place and were scrambling to figure out what to do. There were at least 30 people waiting to get into their rooms when we got here. There's no reservation system in place, it's just a random piece of paper.
2. They force you to download an app to queue songs. This sounds like a good idea in theory until you realize that their app is glitchy and doesn't work half the time. The staff also had to do a full system restart to make things work, so we couldn't even start singing until 10:45
3. They came in at 11:30 and asked us to leave. We were shocked -- we told them we had booked for 2h but he said this was not on record. Why would six of us go to this spot only to sing for an hour?
4. Despite the technical issues that required a full system restart, they never added any time as compensation. So we could only sing about 10 songs for 45 minutes.
5. The mics were horrible -- I mean I had to shout into the mic to be able to hear myself, and this was in a small room meant for 6-8 people.
6. There are NO STAIRS in this place! Expect to wait at least 15 minutes for the elevator on weekends.

Most reviews here are fake -- they had some free drink incentive going on for a while that helped inflate their rating. This has easily been the worst karaoke experience of my life. There are plenty of better spots in KTown and in NYC. Don't waste your time and money here.

googleReviews.author: Jennie Matha
googleReviews.text:
My friend and I recently visited this karaoke spot, and unfortunately, the experience was disappointing due to poor communication and unprofessional service.
When we walked in, we were told it would be $40 for 1–4 people. Since there were only two of us, it already felt a bit unfair, but we agreed. The front desk employee also mentioned there was a $10 minimum — however, he never clarified that it was per person. Once we got to the room (around 6:45), the front desk employee spent some time explaining how to use the table. Shortly after, the server came in to take our order for the minimum. I ordered two drinks that totaled $10, and she then stated it was a $10 minimum per person… which directly contradicted what we had originally been told. That lack of clear communication was frustrating. To make matters worse, when we asked what time our session ended, the front desk employee told us our time had started five minutes earlier — even though he had been in the room using that time to explain things we didn’t need explained. We were never clearly told when our time officially began. He eventually said he would “restart” the time, meaning it would end at 6:50 since we had paid for one hour.
However, at 6:40, not even a full hour.the server abruptly came in, said “this is the last song,” grabbed the iPad, and walked out. It felt rude and completely cut into the time we paid for. When it came time to pay, we were told the tip was already included. Considering the rudeness and consistent miscommunication throughout the visit, that felt extremely unfair. Our original total was supposed to be $40, yet it ended up being $75 with fees. Overall, the environment and service left a bad impression. Clear communication, respect for customers’ time, and transparency with pricing would make a huge difference. Unfortunately, we won’t be returning.

googleReviews.author: Ingrid P
googleReviews.text:
I was a regular customer of Sing Sing St Marks for years but after my most recent experience with them, I will not return. There are other establishments in Ktown with more professional service and competitive pricing.

I reserved a room about one month in advance for a group of 15-20 people. Everything was smooth at the time of booking. I then called the night before the event to confirm and let manager know our party might be slightly larger, and asked if there was a larger room available. They said no, and that the room reserved for us could fit but would be tight. Because of prior good experiences at the venue and room size, I figured it would be okay, even if a little tight. However we were put into a room that could not fit more than 10-12 people comfortably. The room was clearly not appropriate for even the original request for a room for 15-20 people. To make things worse, the room was not heated (so everyone had to wear their coats, adding to the crowding), and the tech was not ready when we arrived with the lights off, microphones off, and monitor not synced with the audio. We had to call the staff back to the room several times at the start of the session.

When we complained about the size and tech issues, the staff was dismissive and said that “tight” was up to interpretation, and it was not their fault if we had different perspectives on this. The staff then offered to divide our party into two rooms which was not the experience we reserved. They did let us know the large room had been booked and if the other party was late, we could have it. However, they told several members of our party different wait times for the large room and eventually said the room would not be available.

We ended up asking to use the public part of the bar, and were told we would only need to pay for drinks purchased at the bar if we did that, with the room charges waived. We appreciated comping the room charge, but in end the staff added a “song fee” per person which was not disclosed to us when relocating to the public part of the bar and we were double charged for several drinks. The other large party also never arrived and still, the large room was not offered to us.

Overall this experience ruined this venue for me despite patronizing it for 10 years. I agree with recent reviews about poor service and feeling uncomfortable with the staff.

googleReviews.author: Danielle P
googleReviews.text:
TERRIBLE KARAOKE SPOT - GO TO KTOWN INSTEAD. This place should be shut down.

The 1 star reviews are all accurate.  Avoid this karaoke spot. Front desk is rude, unhelpful, equipment does not work, and they double book rooms.

Aside from giving us a room that was impossible for a group of 20 to fit (which is how many people it was booked for a month in advance), the front desk spent about ONE HOUR tech troubleshooting. We had to restart our time multiple times (you pay for the room per hour). The mics were NOT working. The music was NOT synced to the lyrics on screen. They told us to squeeze in that room when it was literally impossible, not just tight.  Some of us lapped up or left to try and make it work. It was not comfortable at all and all of us decided to leave the room in the end.

Turns out they double booked the large room (there’s only one) and even when the other party was late for over 45 mins and did not show up, the front desk still did not offer us the room.

We ended up staying in the public bar area, doing karaoke mixed with strangers for what was supposed to be a private party, and was told that we would not be charged for room or karaoke, just for drinks at the bar. Got the bill and they charged per song when they told us otherwise.

DO NOT COME HERE!!! It is not worth the stress and poor experience.

The song selection is vast and caters to all musical tastes, ensuring that every member of your group can find their favorite tunes to belt out. The private rooms are comfortable and well-equipped, allowing you to sing your heart out in a more intimate setting. The sound system is top-notch, delivering crisp and clear audio that makes you feel like a true superstar.

What truly sets Sing Sing Karaoke apart is the exceptional service provided by the staff. They are attentive, friendly, and always ready to assist, making sure your evening is nothing short of fantastic. The drinks menu offers a variety of options to keep your vocal cords well lubricated, and the food choices are equally enjoyable.

Whether you're celebrating a special occasion or just looking for a fun night out, Sing Sing Karaoke is the place to be. It's an experience that will leave you with fantastic memories and a desire to return for more. Don't miss out on the opportunity to create your own karaoke magic in the heart of New York City.

googleReviews.author: Jeffrey Gomez
googleReviews.text:
I decided to go to karaoke for the first time on my birthday. After looking up a plethora of karaoke spots, this is the one I chose and I’m glad I did. I was 100% satisfied.

The reservation process was kind’ve tricky. I started on their website then they contacted me via text.

I made sure to ask as many questions which they answered all of them. Everything was transparent. No hidden fees.

When I arrived they greeted me and had my reservation ready. The room was a good size for my guests. They gave us complimentary water.

Our guided gave us steps to get the karaoke started and told us how to add songs to the queue. Also, the checked in on us like 3 times. The system was easy to use. If you want to get the most bang for your buck then have all the songs you want ready before you arrive.

The song selection was pretty good. Was missing some songs but they have songs up to 2025. There’s also a section of their website to submit songs. Unfortunately it was down the weekend I went. I was still able to get the other songs I wanted.

All my friends were able to enjoy themselves and pick out songs. It was really fun.

When it came time to pay, the price was pretty good for the group. It was under $50. Be mindful for card the max they can take is 2 cards. The price included tax and gratuity. Which I was fine with.

We didn’t feel like drinking. There was no mandatory drink requirement or hidden fees. Which I liked.

I would definitely come back. Didn’t take any pics but I’ll add some videos from our session. Don’t judge lol.

googleReviews.author: Rai Out
googleReviews.text:
I hate to be the negative review on a business i genuinely think is trying to do a good job. Front staff was really awesome, friendly and welcoming.

The biggest gripe I had was with the taller bartender on the night of 1/3. black and curly short hair. Dude had the most disheartening attitude I’ve ever seen in such a positive environment like a karaoke bar. Miserable. It’s the service industry, atleast fake it. From the get go, inquiring about drinks, he just didn’t seem to want to help. He created a very unwelcoming environment for me and my friends. I still treated him nice but jeez.

Next gripe, the open karaoke set-up is less than ideal. The same 3-4 people were up on stage every single song. *But Rai, why didn’t you request a song yourself?* ahaha we did. Me and my friends requested songs, mind you, it costs $3 dollars per song with a minimum card purchase of $11 EACH TIME. For people who don’t carry cash, it’s a bit obsolete in 2025. It felt like there was favoritism, but I’m doubtful. I think the system is just bad. I think if you’re charging for a song, there should be an option to pay a dollar more or something to bump your song up the queue a bit. Or, alternatively, just let there be a dedicated song manager to mix it up a bit. It got so boring watching people never leave the stage singing 5 songs and not knowing the words for 4 of them.

I know I sound bitter, but we waited nearly 3 hours and never had a chance. Luckily there was another bartender, shorter guy, who allowed us to get a refund for the songs we paid for. They were really kind, and that made me feel a little better. Ultimately we still gave up and left.

Closing thoughts: the owners and front staff are awesome, and they have booths so next time I’d try the private booths for my group.

googleReviews.author: Gerald Butler
googleReviews.text:
Came in alone last night and I was just hoping to have a drink and maybe not feel invisible. One bartender, longer hair, was really welcoming at first I really liked his singing and his drinks were really not that well mixed but, honestly, he was really cute so I probably read too much into it. As the night went on, that warmth faded, and it didn’t seem like my very mild advances were reciprocated. Fair enough, but it still felt awkward. The prices are a little too much for the quality of service and drinks anyways.

I also met a bald man who was handsome who seemed part of my type of community. In a painfully earnest moment, I was genuinely hoping he’d become my best friend after all we rap. That energy was very much not returned, and the interaction ended up feeling smug on his end and deeply embarrassing on mine.

I’m fully aware this makes me sound pathetic, and it probably is. Still, the overall vibe felt very insiders-only, which isn’t great when you show up solo and try. The bar itself seems cool — just maybe better if you come with friends or emotional armor. Also smug bartenders is not a great way to run a bar.

googleReviews.author: Naiya Leon
googleReviews.text: I celebrated my 21st birthday here with my friends and our karaoke experience was 100/10! Customer service was amazing , all questions answered, very attentive, and great selection of songs and rooms. Will definitely be coming back again!

googleReviews.author: Seamus O'Sullivan
googleReviews.text: Radio Star Karaoke is one of the best karaoke joints in midtown. Nothing but good vibes here. Both public and private karaoke options. Great personalities like Harry, Danny, and Isaac. Highly recommend this spot if you want to pass time and sing some tunes with lovely people. 10/10

googleReviews.author: Tatum H.D.
googleReviews.text: Wow. These are some of the rudest people I’ve ever met in NYC. My friends and I went the other night to do karaoke, as we thought our other friend was already there and we would meet him. The security guard was extremely rude and harsh, immediate telling some of us to dump out our water bottles. We didn’t mind that part, but the way he said it was uncalled for. Then the employees were EXTREMELY (and I can’t stress it enough) hostile and rude as I tried to communicate with them our situation. They repeatedly said our friend wasn’t there, even before I had shown them a photo or given a name. They said there were no more reservations that evening, when they weren’t even supposed to close until 3 hours from our arrival time. It was very, very clear they didn’t want us there. What a shame too because we would’ve given them good business with the large group I was with. The guy working was slightly nicer than the rest, but that girl with blue hair has a real attitude issue. I’m disappointed because a lot of the other reviews of this place seemed wonderful, but I’ve noticed the more recent reviews echo my awful experience. My friends and I will never come back here. I hope management really shapes up the behavior and compassion of their staff members. If you want a nice experience where staff won’t literally roll their eyes at you, I’d recommend 32 Karaoke or Chorus Karaoke!

The system they have is also a little buggy and we had trouble removing songs and had to just manually skip over them as they came up.

The Radio room was an awesome space (while it says it holds 30, I would not push past 24 adults comfortably)

The Food and Bunch cocktails were Delish, since we were on a time limit/crunch, theatre after, I sent menu to guest ahead of time and RPM's system of order taking and delivery made it all run smoothly

googleReviews.text:
30AUG.2025 This was me, my daughter, and her boyfriends first time and his mom(has been here before).

Lena was awesome in all the information she was telling us. Such a great experience. We only wanted water and that was brought to the room we rented for an hour. The rate was reasonable and worth every cent.

RPM Underground has some cool items inside this building, fully stocked bar, and binds and binds full of music. This is a wonderful way to kick back and have a great time solo, with family, and friends.

googleReviews.text:
I’ve been coming here consistently for about 2 years. The crowds are great when they come! Always a friendly vibe and great underground atmosphere. Joseph has to be one of the greatest bartenders in the city! Always fun when staff joins in on the mic. It’s beautifully decorated with great lighting for some nice photo opportunities.
The song list is extensive and constantly being updated, it’s $3 a song. Trying not to sound bias so the only down side is the drink prizes. As a dive bar regular $5 beers & shots are my weakness.

googleReviews.author: Casey Blake
googleReviews.text: I love a karaoke bar but this one was lacking something extremely important to the overall experience...good sound. Not even decent sound. It was really bad unfortunately. The bartender was really nice but it was really hard to enjoy the bar area. The music was so low that you couldn't really hear it and the mics were so terrible, they didn't pick up sound. Or maybe it was the sound system or receivers that connect to the mics. And when the mics finally got sound, it kept cutting out. I'm sure if all you've experienced was that place, you'd be okay with that bad quality sound but once you've gone to some other places, this just doesn't do it. If they update their audio system, I would love to come back. Right now, I'm going to opt out.

googleReviews.text:
not the best rates (drink prices were insane) but at least they were honest and upfront with the charges. they even explained our bill at the end.

they have a 2-hr minimum stay which isn’t crazy at all. however, make sure you keep track of time (ask them to remind you or set an alarm on your phone) as you will lose yourselves in the singing.

one point I’d like to make is that the process of finding songs and setting everything up through QR codes and phone apps? it’s not the smartest way to do things for karaoke. especially when you’re most likely slightly intoxicated or intend to be. we spent about 15 minutes just trying to navigate the apps & half the songs we wanted, we couldn’t even find.

the $25/person unli drinks deal is a good deal indeed if you can handle your liquor. but the options are limited. we only got vodka mixed with fruit juices throughout and a screwdriver isn’t part of it — which was a little ??? if you know how to make one.

I will still recommend them if the original place you want to go to is not taking walk-ins because the staff are nice and the place is relatively well-kept.

googleReviews.author: Debbie DelValle
googleReviews.text:
This is the second time I reserved a private karaoke room for my 5 friends and I. The first time was pre pandemic. The room rate was $40 per hour for up to 5 people the $8 per hour for each additional person. Pre pandemic  a karaoke room reservation also came with a free 6 pack of beer (not that we are beer drinkers) and bottle service. There was also a food menu to order from. During our first experience, we ordered a bottle of vodka and were provided with mixers to make cosmopolitans. We ordered the appetizer sampler that came with fries, shrimp, chicken nuggets. We reserved the room for 3 hours and extended it one additional hour because we were having so much fun. When the bill arrived, the total came to a little over $367 and we were told if we paid cash we could pay $360 even. It was such a great experience we were looking forward to returning once they reopened after COVID.

Post pandemic the experience was completely different. We came on the Wednesday after Christmas as we were all on break from work.  The karaoke room rate remained the same. However, we were the only ones there so there was only one gentleman working the bar and no one present to attend the kitchen so the kitchen was closed. We were unable to order any food. First disappointment. The second disappointment was that there was no more beer included with the room and no bottle service. Instead they now offer open bar for $22 per person/per hour, or premium open bar for $29 per person/per hour. We opted for the $22per person/ per hour option. We again reserved the karaoke room for 3 hours but stood longer because we decided to order food through Grubhub since we were starving after a few hours. We ordered food and even ordered food for the gentleman attending our group since we felt sorry that he was there working alone. We ended the night 6 hours later. I also have to comment that some of the song lyrics were incorrect and the tune was different than expected on a numbers of songs. We had a great time, but the open bar was an absolute purse drainer. The third and final disappointment………………..the bill was $1089 compared to the $367 we paid the first time which included food. We were not offered any deals like last time.

Overall we enjoyed ourselves since we were in each others company. Being friends for over 25 years, we bring the fun to wherever we go. We were looking forward recreating the memorable experience we had pre pandemic and end the year together. Unfortunately, this experience was a complete 180 compared to the first time. Don’t think we will be coming back.

googleReviews.author: Alex R
googleReviews.text:
OVERCHARGED US! They overcharged us and then denied it when we call them out on it. Let me preface this with a few facts:

A service fee is a fee paid for services rendered, a room fee is a fee paid for a space used by a client, and gratuity is the same as tip and is not mandatory. If you need to claim that tips are necessary for a worker to get a fair wage then the employer is not paying them a fair wage to begin with.

My party and I had a room for an hour and brought less than five drinks. We did our math to know how much the bill would be. Upon settling our bill we were told there was a 'policy mandatory gratuity fee.' Which is NOT thing, that's a fee and calling it anything else is dishonest. Upon calling them out on this they gave us a 5-minute runaround and refused to remove it or allow us to change it (a forced 18% tip) claiming that the boss had to be there to change it and the boss wasn't there (which is a whole other conversation in terms of irresponsible management and disempowerment of employees, if any of that was even true to begin with). Lastly, no one even came to give us a time warning, I had to go out and check and that was the only reason we weren't forced to pay for more time then we planned which would have given them another reason to blind side us.

TLDR; They were trying to overcharge us and when called out on it refused to remove it and gave at most subpar service.

Me and my partner just wanted to sing and have a good time for date but without drinking alcohol but to force people to get drinks just to meet the $10 drink per person and to make us pay 20% gratuity on top of all of this is wild since our server never checked up on us since he left the room and get drop off our water bottles and juices lol.

Try other places

googleReviews.author: Erika Tsimbalov
googleReviews.text: My coworkers and I had a great experience from start to finish.  I was able to book a small private room just one day in advance for a Friday night right after work. The manager, Sam, is highly responsive, friendly, compassionate and was so quick to bring our drinks to the room too, despite him being the only one working for a few hours. The drinks were delicious, especially the lychee spritz mocktail. Although the ramen is the cup of noodles version, it ended up being sooo good. The noodles were so soft and flavorful. I got the spicy one with an egg. I loved it. Sam carefully explained how to use the iPad controller for music selection and it was so much better than flipping through a book!!! It was so easy to use and it had EVERY song we could think of. Advice: use the artist search to find the songs vs by song title. For some reason the song title search didn't work.  But artist search worked perfectly!  The vibe of the overall place is like a colorful quirky dive bar, which can definitely be felt in the bathrooms. Two of the soap dispensers didn't work, but at least one did! And paper towels were plenty, as well as toilet paper and clean toilets.  I desperately needed tea or something hot to drink because I was singing so many songs , and Sam informed me they didnt have any, but then thoughtfully offered hot water with lemon which was perfect. Our room was cozy, clean, and comfortable. Sam even turned on A/C for us because it was a little warm at first.  He really was so helpful and care for us to have the best experience. He even gave us some extra time because we were having such a good time.  Hands down will come back because the management was so wonderful.  One note about the music though: sometimes the words felt off key with how the music was going so it threw us off sometimes but we still managed to stay on track for the most part. The microphones and speakers are pretty loud and very clear.  The iPad controller lets you control volume AND tone/pitch to match your voice.

We had such a great time celebrating my girlfriend’s birthday. Staff was super friendly. Food was nice. Drinks were great karaoke was amazing. Location was very convenient. Nice quick walk from Grand Central terminal.
Not much to complain about. We’ll definitely come back.

So we agreed for just an hour during that hour we could’ve get to enjoy it to the fullest due to the audio issue wasn’t properly set for us my partner had to go out looking for some help which took time in our hour. Then to end it off I let the employee charge my card and they decided to tip themselves 18% tip rather than asking me what I’d like to tip for my experience.

googleReviews.author: Victor Fenton Aguilar
googleReviews.text: My friends and I stumbled across this bar last Saturday when we visited nyc. The vibe seemed good and we were having a good time singing, everything was great until we met the bartenders. The guy in charge of the karaoke was very rude, would only accept bills in cash to take song requests and kept asking people to tip him more to move your song up the queue. We didn’t have cash and asked if we could tip more in the round of shots we were getting to request a song. He said no and told us to get cash from the ATM there, which had insanely high fees. Both him and the woman bartending had a bad attitude and seemed like they didn’t want to be there. After we had gotten 3 rounds of shots for 5+ people (spent about $300) per round and tipped over 15% each time, my friend gave me his card and asked me to get another round on him. I asked him what to tip and he told me just $1 this time since we had spent too much money already. After getting that round, we got joined by more of our friends and I went to get a round of 8 tequila shots. When I asked the bartender for them, he said “I don’t know are you going to tip a dollar this time too?” - wow, complaining about tips to the customer’s face is so unprofessional. I explained that it was my friend’s card and that I had tipped them over $10 on the previous rounds I got, and they both started insulting me and complaining about the tips. Then they moved all songs in Spanish to the bottom of the queue because we are Latinos and had been singing in Spanish - there was other Hispanics there that got their songs moved down because of that. They completely killed our vibe and upset us so we and the Hispanics we met there (9 people total) decided to leave and go to another bar. So the bartenders probably lost the bar a fair deal of business over their tips and bad attitude. Save your money and go somewhere else.

googleReviews.author: Gina Liu
googleReviews.text:
Heard a lot of rave reviews of the bar beforehand, but their karaoke queue system and service left a lot to be desired. Before our party we communicated directly with Winnie’s staff over social media and were told we had a booth reserved for our party. However, when we arrived, the bartenders there refused to let us have a booth and said the communication before was not applicable because *they* did not send the messages …

Besides that, their karaoke request system was disorganized and scammy. The bartenders kept interrupting people singing karaoke songs to ask if people *were really singing* and complaining about the queue of 40 songs. If you want karaoke to run smoothly, there should be a designated staff person running it, so that a queue of 40 songs close to closing time doesn’t happen. Or ask people to write down names on their slips so money can be returned if their song isn’t played. Then one bartender was having a power trip and demanding the mics be returned to the bar after some songs, but not all… really would not recommend overall.

Minor thing: Winnie’s benefits off a lot of Chinese and Asian imagery include tsingtao posters but doesn’t serve tsingtao? Cmon… same goes for showing Asian music videos but playing their own *not karaoke* generic electronic music over it

googleReviews.author: Ctgb
googleReviews.text:
Here’s a personal review in American English for Winnie’s Bar (New York):

Winnie’s Bar – Personal Review

Winnie’s Bar is one of those neighborhood gems that feels both effortlessly cool and undeniably welcoming. From the moment you step inside, the atmosphere is relaxed yet stylish — a perfect blend of laid-back comfort and refined taste. It’s exactly the kind of place you want to return to again and again, whether you’re meeting friends or grabbing a casual drink after a long day.

The vibe here strikes the sweet spot between cozy and lively. The lighting, décor, and music create a warm, inviting energy without ever feeling loud or pretentious. It’s a spot where conversations flow easily and the crowd feels friendly and unforced — a mix of locals, professionals, and visitors alike.

Cocktails at Winnie’s are a standout. They’re thoughtfully crafted, balanced, and creative without being overly complicated. Whether you’re into classics with a twist or something more adventurous, the drink menu delivers. I especially appreciated how consistently great the mixology was from visit to visit — each cocktail felt intentional and well made.

The bar food and small plates are equally satisfying. Perfect for sharing, the menu complements the drinks really well. Every dish I tried had solid flavor and quality — not just bar snacks, but bites worth ordering on their own.

Service is another highlight. Staff are friendly, attentive, and genuinely knowledgeable about the menu — they make you feel welcomed without ever being pushy. It’s easy to get good recommendations and feel confident in trying something new.

Overall, Winnie’s Bar is a perfect blend of good drinks, tasty bites, and a chill yet vibrant atmosphere. A spot I’d recommend for a relaxed night out, date night, or casual catch-up with friends.

googleReviews.author: Keith Nelson Jr
googleReviews.text: Terrible bar. My friend had her phone stolen by someone who was best friends with the bartender. Had it in her pocket the entire time. Once my friend said she was calling the cops, the girl magically found the phone in her pocket, and never said sorry. The bartender also wasn’t apologetic or reprimanding of the person who stole because that’s his friend. He just blamed it on her being drunk. How drunk do you have you to be to not know a phone is vibrating in your pocket when it’s called when you have your phone in your hand? No one apologized because they probably do this all the time. Avoid this place at all costs.

Drinks were not strong at all. Bartender in charge of karaoke would also frequently interrupt people's songs so they could say something about the mics or other unnecessary announcement. Drinks are expensive for what they are! And so are the songs ($1 bills only) (with no guarantee they'll actually be played in order)...avoid!

googleReviews.author: J.
googleReviews.text: Cornerstone Tavern is a cozy, noteworthy gem in the league of sports bars in NYC—whether it be wandering in after a long day in the hustle and bustle, meeting up with friends, catching up on some football, testing your knowledge at trivia nights, and my favorite: karaoke nights! There’s something about belting out bops in a timeless, tavern style venue that takes away the nerves of singing your heart out. With less ego, and more community (contrary to some karaoke spots I’ve been to that literally have patrons who critique how you sing—like, really Ed?), I love how the host makes everyone feel encouraged and comfortable, handing over the mic like a passing of the baton, and supporting every singer along with the crowd. I was so moved in singing November Rain, and these two British lads were so kind and even shook my hand. I had such a wonderful time, and appreciate the times I’ve occasionally found myself at Cornerstone Tavern, with an amazing team of bartenders and staff overall who create quite the legacy in Turtle Bay. These folks work so hard, probably with very long hours, but nonetheless treat their customers like family. When I was getting tired, one bartender Matt even asked if I was ok, while a fellow patron offered to braid my poofy hair. Now that’s community! Thank you all for cheering me up, and creating such an awesome space. Happy Holidays!

I could tell you about Uncle Charlie’s charming atmosphere, the live piano, or the elegant and relaxed vibe of the place… but none of that would be the same without Juan Carlos behind the bar.

Juan Carlos isn’t just a bartender; he’s a master of hospitality. From the very first greeting, he makes you feel right at home with warmth and infectious energy. His remarkable memory for each customer's preferences, his talent for crafting custom cocktails, and his skill in reading the room make him a true star.

I’ve visited many bars, but few have someone like Juan Carlos – professional, attentive, authentic, with a charisma that elevates the entire experience. If you go to Uncle Charlie’s, don’t just come for the music—come for him. I guarantee you’ll end up staying longer than you planned, simply because of the way he makes you feel.

Thank you, Juan Carlos, for making every visit special. You’re the reason I’ll always come back.

googleReviews.text: My wife and I went to Bo Peep Cocktail and Highball Store on Christmas Eve based on recommendations from friends.  And we were simply blown away!!! Everything was amazing.  First of all, we are huge fans of music.  They had different pianists playing and singing songs throughout the night.  You could even submit recommendations for them to play and sing.  Everyone had a great voice and we enjoyed the music.  Also, the servers jumped in on the singing as well.  Our server, Stephanie, was phenomenal.  She provided great service and even made recommendations for us for food and drinks.  She also has an amazing voice and sang a few songs while still serving tables.  Literally!!! She would have a microphone in one hand and sang while she delivered drinks with the other hand.  Absolutely amazing!!! Secondly, the food was phenomenal.  Definitely exceeded our expectations.  We tried the Fried Chicken Sliders, Mini Ceviche Tacos and Buffalo Chicken Pizza.  Everything was delicious.  Third, the drinks were delicious.  We each tried 3-4 different drinks and loved them.  The Professor and Midnight in the Garden were our personal favorites.  Fourth, we loved the ambience and the setup of the bar for the holidays.  It has the speakeasy vibe we enjoy.  Lastly, the service was impeccable.  Honestly, I couldn’t have asked for more.  We thought we would make a quick stop to check this place out and ended up staying there for well over 2 hours.  I’d recommend this place to anyone and we will definitely be back!

googleReviews.author: Connie K. Chung
googleReviews.text:
I’ve been a regular at Den Social Lounge since it first opened. If that gives away that I’m a millennial, then yes, I’m a millennial. I’ve also spent years going out across NYC. K-Town, Meatpacking, LES, West Village, Brooklyn, and venues like Mission, Maru, Somewhere Nowhere, Tao, Public Hotel, Marquee and Le Bain etc etc. With that perspective, I think a lot of the negative reviews here are missing some important context.

Security’s role is to manage safety, capacity, and overall flow of the venue. They are not there to host or entertain guests at the door. That’s standard across NYC nightlife, regardless of neighborhood. If you’ve spent time going out in other parts of the city, you know that bouncers are rarely overly friendly. That’s not unique to Den. It’s how nightlife operates. The complaint about a security/staff personnel prohibiting you from holding your drink over the railing is hilarious - it's called liability. If you drop the drink and it injures a patron that's standing below, the venue is at fault...not you so yeah, security was just doing his job.

Waiting in line or not being admitted is also not unusual at a popular venue. Lines happen everywhere. Being turned away at the door also happens everywhere. Showing up earlier when doors open (10:30pm) and not at peak time (12am-1am), dressing appropriately, being coherent, and treating staff with basic respect goes a long way. That’s true at Den and at any club or lounge in the city.

I’ve also worked front of house before, and I can say firsthand that patience and politeness dramatically improve everyone’s experience. Most issues at the door come down to attitude or dress code, not the venue.

Want a better nightlife experience? Learn some basic nightlife etiquette and build relationships at establishments that you frequent often including the host, promoter and security. It's not that hard people.

Den has consistently delivered a good vibe, strong music, and is a well-run operation. The staff does their job well, and the experience reflects that.

Caviar toasts – 5/5: Fan favorite for sure!! The butter on the toast paired perfectly with the caviar.

Potato balls – 4.25/5: More classic, but still really good and comforting.

Fries – 5/5: Possibly some of the best fries I’ve ever had — we ordered so many more.

And ofc, the cocktails here are top tier using top shelf liquor which you can tell!

googleReviews.author: Tim Griffiths
googleReviews.text:
From the outside Cassidys really doesn't look anything special, it looks like just an ordinary bar, an Irish Pub, a bit of a dark and dingie front door and entrance area and indeed it's not anything special but it knows what it is and does what it knows very well; that's good beer, good hospitality and decent food for your money.

But once inside it's a warm, friendly and is clearly a really popular bar that has plenty of atmosphere with very welcoming staff to boot. The decor is plain and simple, with tables, bar stools and high-tops with the walls adjourned with old signs, TVs showing sports and themed pictures.

The menu is straight forward, simple and quite basic but it's reasonably priced and from what we had it wasnt bad. I had buffalo wings whilst my wife had the French onion soup 🍲,  which she really enjoyed. Great choice of beers.

The service was really good. The restrooms were clean.

Level 10 Google reviewer with over 1,200 reviews with 2 million views plus 14,000 photos with more than 60 million views and still going strong 💪.

Check out my other reviews 🌟 🌟 🌟 🌟 🌟.

googleReviews.author: Stephanie Martin
googleReviews.text: Came here on a Sunday, early in the evening. Love the atmosphere, very intimate and cozy. The cocktails were lovely and the food was nicely flavored. Me and my two friends shared our dishes with each other. All dishes were yummy but my fav were the green curry and the thai fried wings (meat was tender and not dry). They were also on point with the spice level we requested. Also liked that they weren't skimming in the thai basil on the krapow. However, the cheeseburger spring rolls could have used more filling. The boozy bubble tea was cool, liked how the thai iced tea wasn't too sweet but the booze part lacked a bit. The regular cocktails were actually really enjoyable, all very refreshing. At the end they gave us a complimentary mochi donut which omg we loved and we aren't fans of mochi donuts but I'd def come back for these. Staff was really friendly and helped take photos for us. Overall good experience.

googleReviews.text: Threw my husbands surprise 30th birthday here and it was phenomenal! Very professional with a contract and deposit securing the date. I was in contact with the owner regularly asking questions via text and she was able to help me coordinate everything I needed! The cost was well worth it and she allowed me to have my guests pay for themselves rather than have my card down for an open bar. The karaoke system was updated and modern and my friends and family had a great time! I would definitely recommend this to anymore in the UWS looking for a private party. We also got appetizers which were tasty and plenty for my guests.

googleReviews.author: Debisree Ray
googleReviews.text:
I visited this lounge on a rainy, chilly Sunday evening with someone to spend some time together. I didn’t expect it to be crowded, but to my surprise the place was full and lively. It was noisy, as lounges usually are, but not so loud that we couldn’t have a conversation — just the right amount of energy so it didn’t feel dull.

We started with drinks. He ordered a glass of Guinness, and I chose one of their cocktails — something with rum and a citrusy twist. I don’t remember the exact name, but it was surprisingly good. I’m not a big drinker, so I tend to prefer cocktails where the flavor is elevated and not dominated by alcohol, and this one was perfect.

The best part — and a pleasant surprise — was that with every drink you buy, you get a ticket for a free personal pizza. They had a proper Italian-style oven in the back, and they were making fresh, individual cheese pizzas. The one we got was hot, simple, and delicious. I was hungry, so we finished it quickly — so quickly that I even forgot to take a picture!

The lounge also seemed to have pool tables and other things to enjoy if you’re hanging out with friends. The bartender was friendly, the atmosphere was upbeat, and overall we had a really nice time.

Seventh Heaven is literally my favorite bar I've ever been to. Not only is the karaoke fun, but the drinks are incredible, the bartenders are lovely, and they have instant noodles!!
Special shoutout to Midnight who, when I asked them for a straw to try and help my friend untie their shorts, instead decided to come over and help untie my friend's shorts themselves! We were struggling, so Midnight saved us from having to cut the string off my friends shorts so she could pee 😭
Also some people mention in their reviews that some songs get bumped to the back of the Karaoke queue. I'm not sure exactly how it works, but it seems as though songs added by people who haven't sung yet get priority, and it's the people who have gone up a few times that get bumped to the back of the queue. This system, in my opinion, helps keep things fair and makes sure everyone gets a chance!!

When our food was ready, we came back to the bar and noticed two open seats. One had what looked like old, half-eaten food sitting in front of it, but no one was there. We sat down to eat the food we had just ordered. Shortly after, a woman with black hair — who I’m assuming is a manager — approached us and instead of saying the seat was taken, she said, “Yeah, you’re not gonna sit here.” I immediately apologized and explained that we didn’t realize the seat was occupied and that the food looked old, and I had even moved slightly to avoid sitting directly in front of it. She repeated, “Yeah, you’re not gonna sit here.”

I completely understand that running a busy bar isn’t easy, but there’s a more professional and welcoming way to communicate that a seat is reserved or taken — especially to new customers who had been enjoying the atmosphere up to that point. The interaction changed the tone of the night for us. We boxed up our food and left shortly after.

It’s unfortunate because the vibe and live music were great, but customer service matters just as much. I don’t think we’ll be returning.

googleReviews.author: Paige Austin
googleReviews.text: I will never return. I was there and the bartender Jackie was very rude and inattentive and more focused on smoking cigarettes and yelling at her coworkers and my friend for sitting in her seat she had occupied while on the clock and bartending. Who does that… you’re working. And when I said something to I assume the owner he completely ignored me. Food was alright but on the pricier side. Just a strange encounter. Again I won’t return

googleReviews.author: Eric Marlinski
googleReviews.text: Saw the sign on Walden Ave. and on a whim we decided to order food to go. Wife ordered a chicken quesadilla and I went with a chicken salad. We also ordered the pretzels. Wife's quesadilla was huge and delicious. Our teenage daughter tried a slice and begged us to order her one soon. The only small complaint was more salsa and sour cream on the side for a quesadilla that size. My salad was very, very fresh. The salad was crisp and all the veggies and chicken were great. The salad was also huge! The pretzels were fine. Overall, we were very satisfied and will be ordering again soon!

googleReviews.author: Maureen Adolf
googleReviews.text:
The wings were awesome. Try the Kangaroo Lou wings- medium sauce with herbs.
Also tasty, the honey garlic. Served hot and crispy.

address: 5175 Broadway #1, Depew, NY 14043
about: Nickel City BrewZ is a brewery in Depew, New York. It holds a 5.0-star rating from 64 Google reviews and is verified on Google. Guests come for alcohol, beer and onsite services. googleReviews.author: Jeffery Bouton
googleReviews.text:
Nickle City Brewz in Depew is one of the spots I actually enjoy grabbing a beer — and the fact that it’s right down the road makes it dangerously convenient, and it’s welcoming, let’s be honest: there’s a crew of regulars who seem to have assigned seating. The good kind of regulars — the ones who’ll slide over, talk nonsense, and make you feel like you’ve been coming there for years.

They’ve got the best tap selection in town, no argument. Always rotating, always interesting, and occasionally strong enough to make you forget you still have responsibilities.

Brian keeps the place running smooth without ever acting like he’s trying. And Cliff? Cliff is the mad scientist behind the bar, cooking up special concoctions that somehow always hit. Just ask what he’s mixing at the moment. (Not my “go to” but a lot of folks love it).

Best part? If you kick a keg, that beer is FREE — but you have to ring the cowbell. It’s the rules. The whole bar erupts like you just scored a touchdown, and suddenly you’re the main character for a minute.

And when it’s coming down outside? Nickle City Brewz is the perfect spot to watch a snowstorm roll in. Beer in hand, windows frosted, everyone half-settled in for the long haul — it just hits different. Not to mention the sunsets, bring your shades.

Good people, great beer, and zero nonsense. Nickle City Brewz feels like home… if home had louder cowbells and way better views during a blizzard.

googleReviews.author: Nick
googleReviews.text:
A hidden gem in a city of beer.
Above all friendly owners. Always make time to say hello and find out how you're doing. Remebers ever face that comes in.
On the business end, 3 dozen beers on tap and many more in cans.
Build your own 4 pack and have them crack one open for you and take a seat.
It would be a large bar but with social distancing you can sit a few groups there. A few booths and some high tops as well.
Big screens for the games, snacks available and a clean spacious gathering spot.
Trivia on Wednesday nights.

Here for special events

googleReviews.author: Brigid Maloney
googleReviews.text: Great place for a beer lover to stop in and try something local and new. Had a great chat with the proprietor, Brian, who was pouring cold ones behind the bar in a Sabres jersey. He knows a lot about local breweries and is really fun to chat with! Plus you've gotta love a business owner who sticks with the Sabes through the tough times.

googleReviews.author: Chris Polus
googleReviews.text: Great little place to grab a beer. They have 40 plus beers/ciders to choice from. Not much of a menu. More of a beer place. Prices are reasonable and their happy hour prices are even better.

googleReviews.author: Wendy Gee
googleReviews.text: I had a birthday party last night at Nickel City Brewz and it was perfect. A comfortable atmosphere with an amazing selection of local beer and ciders. Brian and Cliff were great behind the bar and with setting us up for our party. All of our guests, most of who had never been there, were pleasantly surprised. They loved the beer selection and just the overall feel. You had tables of people playing board games, they have corn hole boards, you can hear music, but you can still have a conversation without screaming. Just a great time!

googleReviews.author: Tashia Carron
googleReviews.text: After a little bit of confusion regarding a reservation, Keglers was able to accommodate our party for the St. Patrick's Day Party with Throwback Jack. Our server was very nice and accommodating all evening. She did a great job taking care of us considering she had another large party she was also taking care of. The dining room here isn't huge, nor is the staging area for the band but it works. Their policy for parties over 8 requires a $25.00 deposit when your reservation is made, and 20% gratuity for the total check. They will not split checks for parties over 8. We enjoyed our evening here for Throwback Jack. They rocked the place!!

googleReviews.author: steve c
googleReviews.text: Keglers, located inside Transit Lanes, has fantastic food. That's the bottom line. I never would have suspected it.  When I think of food at bowling alleys, I think of roller dogs, and pizza that's been on an aluminum tray in a rotating display for 3 days.  Keglers will dispel all of those thoughts for you, if you have similar fears or apprehensions.  This is probably the best. Reuben in buffalo.

googleReviews.author: Sean Stanton
googleReviews.text: I called at 10:30 and asked how much longer they were open. They answered saying they were open until midnight. We arrived at the bar at 10:40 and when we sat they immediately told us they weren’t serving anymore. Not sure why they rejected us when 10 minutes earlier they said they were open for another hour and a half. It wasn’t even crowded. Will never come back horrible service. They could’ve told me on the phone they weren’t gonna serve us 10 minutes later. Absolutely horrible to prospective customers for no reason.

googleReviews.author: Todd Beyer Jr
googleReviews.text: I had order take out for the first day of lent ordered a fish fry which was good but the portion of the sides were a little insulting especially for paying 18 dollars for the meal and a dollar for the box. It’s almost like they are looking to save a buck. I had probably a dozen tator tots and the presentation wasn’t all there. I even gave a courtesy call and left a voicemail and never received a call back. So here I am leaving a review. My coworkers were excited to see what I brought back and when I opened the box that laughed and said I believe you got ripped off. I don’t believe I will go back there unless this is rectified. Which is sad because I only work 3 minutes down the street and I was hoping for a new lunch spot.

A great experience!!!  Thank you Lindsey!!!

googleReviews.author: Dr.Patrick
googleReviews.text: I am commencing my second season participating in pool tournaments. The pool hall maintains a welcoming atmosphere. The cuisine offered is ofhigh quality. The venue is consistently crowded; however, it remains an excellent location to play on top-tier tables, and even their house cue sticks are of satisfactory quality.

googleReviews.author: alexia
googleReviews.text: Went here last night for the first time with a small group and had a lot of fun! We weren’t fully sure how the place worked cause we passed the place and decided to stop by and once inside we quickly got assigned a table, but now we know they charge on a time basis per person. But split between the group it was relatively inexpensive for how long we stayed! The food and drinks were good and staff consistently walked around making sure we were okay. The music they played for a Saturday night was great too! Great mix of every genre! And the place was clean. Would come back again!

googleReviews.author: Anonymous
googleReviews.text: Had an absolutely phenomenal experience at Raxx Pool Room, and Lae and Sarah were the true stars of the night. Their level of hospitality, professionalism, and genuine kindness was beyond impressive. From the moment we walked in, they made us feel like valued guests and went above and beyond in every possible way to ensure we had an amazing time. googleReviews.author: Elissa Rubin, M.D.
googleReviews.text: Last night we celebrated my 50th birthday at the Recovery Room.  I cannot say enough wonderful things about this place.  The owners are amazing and they made sure the party ran perfectly.  They decorated for me, provided all the food and snacks, and the DJ was amazing.  The manager, Andrea, was so sweet and helped me plan everything in advance.  Andrea and Freddy, the bartenders, made sure everyone was enjoying the open bar.  The DJ was great and let me choose the type of music that makes me happy.  My friends all loved him.   Every staff member was attentive and made sure my guests and I were having a great time.  They provided a 3 hour private party for me.  The food was also delicious.  I highly recommend the Recovery Room.

googleReviews.author: Bren R
googleReviews.text:
Always a fun time at this place! We originally started coming here for the karaoke, which is an absolute blast—especially with our KJ, Stump Master Flex! 🎤😄

The food is fantastic. My favorites are the Guinness sliders and the cauliflower crust pizza—always on point. We recently decided to check out Sunday bingo and, once again, zero disappointment. So much fun!

The owners are always present, incredibly nice, and truly hospitable, which makes the experience even better. And bonus points for the location—it’s right across from the Mineola LIRR station, perfect for anyone coming after work or choosing to be safe.

Highly recommend!

googleReviews.author: Alisha Islam
googleReviews.text:
Freddie was hands down one of the best bartenders I’ve ever had. From the moment we walked up, he was welcoming, attentive, and genuinely cared about making sure we had an amazing experience. He didn’t just pour drinks he crafted them. Every cocktail was perfectly balanced, flavorful, and made with intention.

What really stood out was how much he went out of his way for us. He took the time to ask what we liked, made thoughtful recommendations, customized drinks to our taste, and made sure everything was exactly how we wanted it. You can tell he takes real pride in his work. Even while staying busy, he never rushed us and kept such positive energy the entire time.

Freddie’s professionalism, creativity, and warm personality made the night so much better. He truly elevated the entire experience and made us feel taken care of. Honestly, the only reason we’ll come back is for him. If you’re lucky enough to have Freddie behind the bar, you’re in great hands. Absolute top tier service and incredible drinks. Highly recommend.

googleReviews.text: A cool local bar. our waiter/bartender was so sweet 😊 wish I could remember her name.  We had mozzarella sticks, dirty tater tots, and teriyaki garlic wings. Portions were big ! Flavor on point. We had Jack and cokes that were perfect ! May not look like anything when you walk in, but don't judge a book by its cover! I almost did, and I'm glad I didn't.  The tables had all New york sports teams. Sorry, I missed that because I would have picked the Knicks one, lol.  Thank you for a great time and great bar food.

googleReviews.author: Tony Bee
googleReviews.text: I've been to this bar twice and twice I've been disappointed. I had high hopes because so many people speak highly of this place, not sure what they experienced but this wasn't true for me. My first experience was for a quick beer, ordered a beer on tap, nothing fancy and immediately knew something was off about the taste of the beer but I drank it and left upon completion. My second chance I decided to grab a drink and some food, but let me tell you was I disappointed... I again ordered the same beer as my previous visit giving the benefit of the doubt and yet again it was flat and sour. I'll give credit to the bartender and server who by the way was the only worker in-site for the whole bar, who noticed I hadn't had my beer and offered another  suggesting he knew the beer wasn't popular and had complaints before. Upon obtaining my second beer I took a sip and to my disgust was an indescribable green/brown blob. I wish I could tell you what it was but to my dismay I'm not sure if it was a bug, mold, or snot. I was so disgusted my stomach churned and wanted to throw up. My immediate thought was to ask for water but at that point I trusted nothing that didn't come from a sealed bottle. I ordered boneless wings, something so simple how can you screw up, I mean cmon I was expecting them to come from a bag frozen, but geez what did I receive... battered chicken cutlets cut into thin pieces that were so tough it was like jerky. The menus were made on excel and printed covered by the staples store plastic paper protectors, and the specials were written in sharpie on a paper and photo copied. Listen I don't mind this from a place undergoing a revamp, or to put on newly added menu items, but for a place that has been around a long time it's just plain embarrassing to not have actual menus. This place may have been a great bar at one time but it's clear to me the owners have given up as it's in dire need of updating, repairs and a total cleaning.

googleReviews.author: steff overbeck
googleReviews.text: We had a lovely experience enjoying seafood at this spot, with a fantastic location overlooking the bay. The view of the sunset was truly breathtaking and added to the ambiance of the meal. However, one downside was the use of plastic cutlery, cups, and plates. It detracted from the overall dining experience and seemed excessive, especially when enjoying such fresh seafood. Switching to more sustainable or reusable options would greatly enhance the experience. Overall, great food and views, but the plasticware left room for improvement.

googleReviews.author: Arthur
googleReviews.text:
I did not enjoy my lunch here. Our server messed up twice, once bringing food that we didn't order, so we had to chat with the manager, and then did it again a second time.

The lobster bisque that I had was below average.

The crab cake had fake crab, which can be OK, but the menu should at least mention this or call it krab cake. Not that I could tell, anyway, because it was so bready. It was more like a bread crumb cake.

I got the scallops for my main, and the scallops were inedible. Absolutely rubber, like chewing an eraser.

I decided, since I'm still hungry, to get a lobster roll. That's about the only thing that I liked here, and why I left 2 stars instead of 1. It was a good size, it tasted good, and the price, while high, is kind of normal for lobster rolls. The cabbage slaw they came with was way too sweet, though, but the fries were thin and crispy and good.

Overall, I won't be coming back, and I can't say that I recommend this place, but if you're going here anyway, then get the lobster roll.

googleReviews.author: Mark Netzer
googleReviews.text: Such a unique set up. I've never been to a restaurant bar that not only had its own boat slips but an enclosed, private sandy beach area for patrons to chill, have a drink and watch the kiddos play. We got the fried clams and they were as good as they get. Super unique food delivery system too...they give you the standard buzzer thingy but you put it into a credit card looking thing attached to your table and it acts like a gps for the servers to bring your food out. Parking is extremely limited so plan on cruising around for a bit to find a spot. Public parking is available off of the main road near some basketball courts and is less than a 5 min walk. Follow it up with ice cream located on the main road near the public parking area!

We asked how many mussels you get and she made a face at us and copped an attitude saying she didn’t know. We only asked because we are not from here. The non-seafood items are very overpriced and we have to use an ATM to tip. I am not very happy to be charged an ATM fee to take care of our bartenders!
