Cool atmosphere, decor, and really a large place with three main areas for music/ comedy I'm guessing. I went at 5pm on a weekday so it was nice and quiet. They played tasteful music. 33% off happy hour when the food and drinks are already priced nicely makes this a go-to for me next time I'm in Columbia! Very nice bartender too.

googleReviews.author: Jacob Jordan King
googleReviews.text:
Art Bar is a great spot in the Vista with a fun mix of solid food and drinks 🍹🍔 The atmosphere is one of the main draws, and it works really well for a casual night out.

Useless Trivia each week is a definite highlight 🧠🎉 - it’s always a good time and brings a lot of energy to the place.

Service can be a bit inconsistent depending on who’s working behind the bar. Some bartenders are excellent and really elevate the experience, while others feel like they’d rather be anywhere else, which can take away from it a bit.

Still, it’s a fun, reliable spot overall and easy to keep coming back to 👍

googleReviews.author: John Doe
googleReviews.text:
Art Bar's a really fun bar, even if it's a little bit outside of my comfort zone! I loved going on karaoke night, it was so much fun watching everybody go all-out and having the crowd sing along. The ambiance was really unique as well, for the first time in Columba I felt like I was getting the real Discoteque experience. I loved how neon the lighting was, it really accentuated the aforementioned disco vibe.

The one negative thing I have to say about it was that most (but not all) of the bartenders were very arrogant, and made it seem like an inconvenience to be asked to make a drink. Two of the bartenders didn't even speak when I asked for my drinks, and just made them in awkward silence, and still didn't say anything when I thanked them for it. Another one made a cocktail, and didn't even bother to mix it, which was kind of weird.

I debated between giving Art Bar three (3) or four (4) stars based on the service, but I ultimately went with four (4). However, had the service been better, Art Bar would've definitely been a 5-star experience!

googleReviews.author: S White
googleReviews.text:
So first and foremost, if this review was ONLY for the food, it would be a five stars. I was pleasantly surprised in the best way it was so good.  I was there today for Yalloween (which was awesome).  I had a pimento burger (subbed veggie) with the fry basket. I did order a fried egg but the girl taking my order didn’t add it.  She is the main reason I took stars (I give her a 2/5) as her demeanor was very rude and dismissive.  She made me feel out of place.  This is NOT how she treats everyone because she was quite nice and accommodating to the people in front of me who appeared to be regulars.

Here’s a tip:  if you want more regulars be nicer to the new people.  I like the food and seating otherwise.

(After I got my food, I found I needed a fork and she did get me one after a short wait.)
She told me the total was $19.80 ($18 + $1.80) but it ended up being $20.49. I assumed perhaps there was an upcharge for using debit; however, she didn’t say, and it wasn’t posted.  So my second assumption was she thought I wasn’t going to tip so gave herself one instead and thought I wouldn’t notice. I left a smaller tip than my norm due to her demeanor ($1.51) which I guess she can add to that $.69 she had to have.  I attached the receipts for reference.  If anyone wants to complain about the tip, keep in mind, she only took the order and payment, not make it, expo it, or serve it. Any tip would be generous in this case.  I am a tipper most of the time having worked in the service industry before even to the not so great workers.

Here’s another tip:  assuming someone isn’t going to tip well and treating them poorly is going to fulfill your expectations. Treating them well may surprise you.

The guy outside walking around in an art bar shirt passing out fries wasn’t a peach either when I inquired about where to get some; however, it was hectic, and I can understand that much better and doesn’t have a real bearing on this review other than making me wonder if this is the culture of the place.

Would I return?  Only if invited out with friends, but not likely on my own.

ETA:  So I read through the other reviews and wow...I am a person of color and seeing so many reviews regarding off treatment of POCs was interesting.  I did not initially get that "ick" because the people in front of me that seemed to be regulars?  It was an interracial couple and the girl was super cool and nice with the guy who was black.  I did not initially think my race was a factor because of that, but I did not feel like I belonged all the same.  A lot of my artist friends come here and I figured I would come with them if invited but now, I won't come back at all.  Food and overall atmosphere aside, why can't everyone be welcome and not just the regulars?

googleReviews.author: Thomas Jacobs
googleReviews.text: They have the best wings I’ve ever had.  Steve takes great pride in everything that comes out of the kitchen.  Jessie and all the staff are always great.  The Art Bar is a Columbia institution.

googleReviews.author: Carla Rankin
googleReviews.text: I enjoyed myself. No complaints of the service. It’s more of a casual hangout than a sophisticated venue if you are into low-key spots. Private rooms for group karaoke (sound system and song list needs updating) if the main floor isn't your thing/you are shy.

googleReviews.author: James McCallum
googleReviews.text: This place is almost a spot out of a quirky sit com or mystery drama a la Twin Peaks or My Name Is Earl.  It's a karaoke bar with Asian fusion food. In a strip mall.  It has karaoke in the main room, but also had private areas. I got the feeling there are s lot of regulars, some of whom are fantastic singers, others of whom have tons of enthusiasm.  It's a whole lot of fun. The karaoke selection is good, though the interface is a little clunky. It has a huge number of unique cocktails as well as beer.  The staff and regulars are friendly and completely non-judemental.  The food was surprisingly excellent, though they were out of the first two things I tried to order. It's comfort food with a Japanese flair.  Definitely worth going.

googleReviews.author: Candace Capaldi
googleReviews.text: So, we are in our 70's , TLC time for us , a getaway, bf is a retired Elvis impersonator, during Covid all gigs stopped...he had one bad ear, totally deaf in that ear, other ear progressively got worse, when all opened up again there were to be no more shows for Bobby J as Elvis. GOOGLE this guy . So every once in awhile we go to Karaoke, this time singing Bobby J  kind of faltered and  I was dying inside for him. BUT, Bobby the bartender at this bar was so very kind, the Karaoke guy tolerant, the customers , AMAZING!! Ty for those who applauded this man who since 1997 kicked ass everywhere from here in SC , NC , and the only Elvis in Key West where he entertained at the Bull and Whistle for ten years, and also in NJ , NY, even Venesuela , all over the country, he's been on the Today Show, several talk shows, look it up.... its all there on Google, so anyways, he kind of was off key and not  so perfect anymore there at this place, but damn if he did not get respect !!! Awesome people , good people . Tears.... thank you from , the girl with Elvis..as I am known ha.....

googleReviews.author: Andrew Warren
googleReviews.text:
Whenever I'm in Columbia, I always stop by for some karaoke and good vibes. As the self proclaimed "Karaoke King" this is by far my favorite place of all time, simply based on the atmosphere.

I wish I knew the names of the staff members because they deserve a shout out. The male bartender got on stage and did one of my favorite songs with me... and he KILLED IT!!! The female bartender sang a few songs with her whole chest! Thanks to her, new songs have been added to my playlist.

I love the audience engagement. I can't sing to save my life but I enjoy doing it.

googleReviews.author: Ayshia Bauldwin
googleReviews.text:
We clearly came out a very calm night, but this is a very nice full bar and karaoke spot.
There is a full bar with everything you could wish for.

There is also a stage with everything a karaoke person could need, including multiple televisions that showed the karaoke lyrics.

I would recommend coming here!! I will be back.

googleReviews.text: We got there around 8 on Saturday when they opened. The atmosphere was laid back at first, then around 10ish the dj comes. googleReviews.author: Jay Flourish
googleReviews.text:
I had an amazing dining experience at Truth of Columbia! I ordered the Teriyaki/Hibachi Chicken Plate, and everything was cooked to order, hot, fresh, and full of flavor. The chicken was tender with a perfect glaze of teriyaki sauce, and the portion size was just right. The veggies were crisp and well-seasoned, and the rice tied it all together nicely.

I also tried the Philly Cheesesteak Eggrolls for the first time, and they did not disappoint! The wrapper was perfectly crispy, and the inside was hot, steamy, and packed with flavor. There’s a special dipping sauce that comes with them—I definitely recommend giving it a try as it adds a great extra kick to the rolls.

Great vibes, solid food, and fast, friendly service. I’ll definitely be back.

googleReviews.author: Jake Neurer
googleReviews.text:
4.5 ⭐ Fun spot to catch live jazz but the cocktails were subpar for the price.

$5 cover charge for live music the night I stopped by, and they accepted cash or card. The jazz was lively and rotated different players as the set went on.

Classic margarita was served in a plastic cup and stired. Menu stated it had lime juice, salt, blue agave and was $12 - tasted like sour mix, no salt on the rim, and I was charged $15. Old fashioned had no cherry, no orange garnish, and stirred with a straw as well (charged over $15). Considering the cover charge, these prices are not worth the drinks. Better off getting beers. Otherwise I had great experience with the music and overall vibe at the Joint

googleReviews.author: Tameika Denise
googleReviews.text: Enjoyed my first time visit,  with my girl friend,  to listen to AP&Soulful Touche'. The lounge is nice, laid back vibe,  but definitely on the smaller side. It provides a bit of intimacy though for a date night 😉. Staff was nice and they have a refreshing complimentary water station at the bar. Will be back!

googleReviews.author: Cypher Goddess
googleReviews.text:
The Joint isn't just a jazz club, it's the perfect, intimate epilogue to our date nights. It's become our cherished tradition, and honestly, the best way to let the evening's magic linger.
​From the moment you step in, the atmosphere is pure, unpretentious romance. It's wonderfully small and intimate, making every note from the stage feel like it's played just for you.
​Our order is always the same, a dirty martini for me and a Bud Light for my love (a perfect, happily mismatched pairing, just like us!). But the real draw is the live music, which is consistently an absolute treat.
​On our last visit, the blues band had me utterly captivated. Closing my eyes, I could feel the music in my soul, it was the kind of deep, soulful sound that makes you want to slow drag and let the rhythm take you completely away. It's truly a place where you can feel the heart of the music.
​If you're looking for an authentic, cozy spot with fantastic live acts and the perfect vibe to end a night with your love, look no further than The Joint. It’s a gem.

googleReviews.author: Robbie Caddell
googleReviews.text: Excellent live music venue, but tonight the sound guy asked me to move from the front of the stage and stand in the reception area side-stage. This was after the band had asked for people to come up and dance for the last several hours. Previously, I was one of 3 dancing up front, but I went to the bar to get the lead singer a shot she had requested. When I got back, I gave her the shot and I was the only one up front. I knew that I was a white guy in a predominantly black establishment, but I felt very welcome until that happened, so I left. Boo, old ornery sound guy, boo.

googleReviews.author: Ponyo Patel
googleReviews.text: Order the mango slush with vodka! This was truly one of the best places we visited for entertainment in Charleston. The vibes were great. The people were kind. Karaoke was amazing. There were no private rooms, but singing in front of a bunch of people you don't know cannot be beat. Got pizza afterwards at the pizza shop just a short walk from here. Came back and sang a little more.

googleReviews.author: C BO
googleReviews.text: Absolutely love this place! We booked a table for my son's 21st birthday and it was perfect! This is an extremely popular spot, so come early or bring some patience. There will be a line, but it is worth the wait. The staff made sure to make us feel like we had been regulars for years. I don't care if you are a local or a visitor, you HAVE to hit this spot for a few cold beers, frozen drinks and hot tracks!

googleReviews.author: Linsey McFarlin
googleReviews.text: The bar itself was a great atmosphere and the bartenders were great. We were visiting from out of state for a special occasion. We asked around for the best karaoke bar and were told Bangkok was the place to go. We got there early at 9:30pm. It wasn’t busy and we put in 4 songs one for each person in our group. As time went by the bar filled up and our songs never came up. The host kept saying it wasn’t our turn. THREE hours went by and nothing. Finally the host came over she said she moved us up since we had a special occasion. A local told us in order to get your song played you have to PAY the host to get it played. Sure enough that was the case. People were giving her cash to get their song played. This is KARAOKE and supposed to be fun for everyone and laid back. To have to PAY to have a karaoke song played is just INSANE and so disappointing when we were looking forward to a fun night out. This host was also singing her own songs when people were still signed up. She was rude and is taking advantage of people and taking money for simple karaoke. Not okay. When we called her out she said she wasn’t accepting money and it was in order of when it was received. Yet a group of guys who came in ONLY 10 minutes prior already sang. When we called her out she had nothing to say and walked away. Comical.

googleReviews.author: Sharaya Smith
googleReviews.text:
I didn't get anything to eat while I was there on Sunday, but let me tell you. . . A time was had!

I spoke to the gentleman at the bar first and he was so kind. He told me not to be nervous about singing, which I was because the crowd seemed to be familiar with each other and I didn't want to be an outsider.

Glad I listened because I had an amazing time with some pretty amazing people!

The guy manning the karaoke list was also really cool and had to put up with alot.

I'm going to try and make my way over at least one more time before I leave.

googleReviews.author: Lexi Ribaya
googleReviews.text: this is the place you want to be if you love karaoke and having a good time!! it’s not your typical karaoke place. no need to rent a room or call all of your people. go alone and make a bunch of friends or bring your friends too! but get ready to sing to a crowd!! they have frozen drinks which i loveeee, you can add liquor or just enjoy as is! (non alcoholic) not to mention DJ Red  makes sure to maintain the vibes every time and NEVER disappoints! feeling shy? she will hop on the mic with you! need a hype girl? she’s right behind or next to you (depending on where you’re standing and singing!) truly the best place EVER. i take all my friends and family when they visit and they always can’t wait to come back to go back!!

address: 354B King St, Charleston, SC 29401, USA

about: Burns Alley Tavern is a bar in Charleston, South Carolina. It holds a 4.5-star rating from 681 Google reviews. This lively watering hole offering bites, games & TVs in unfussy surrounds draws students & locals. Find current hours, directions, and more on KaraokeNearMe.org.

googleReviews.author: John Doe
googleReviews.text: Burns Alley was such a fun time! The bar was packed to the brim, with everybody vibing and having a great time. Despite the fact that the bar was packed, the bartenders were awesome and always made sure that I was good on drinks and doing alright. The DJ that was there was great as well, as he kept playing throwback and contemporary hits that had everybody rocking out. Finally, I loved the location of the tavern, as it was an easy place to leave and walk a short distance to another bar or restaurant. The one (1) small downside was that there was a $10 cover, whereas other similar bars nearby didn’t have one that night. Even with the cover, I’d still recommend dropping in to Burns Alley for a fun night!

googleReviews.author: Brownbiggy
googleReviews.text:
Burns Alley Tavern has a very unique atmosphere, almost like a piece of history is etched into its walls. It’s tucked away in an alley, which gives it a bit of a hidden gem feel. The dim lighting, graffiti-covered walls, and overall dive bar aesthetic make it seem like a cool place to hang out. It definitely has character, and I can see why some people love it.

However, my experience was far from great. The biggest issue was the service—the server was unexpectedly rude for no reason. There was no warmth, no friendliness. A place like this should have a welcoming vibe, but instead, it just felt uninviting.

On top of that, the prices were disappointing. I paid $13.50 for two normal beers, which didn’t feel justified for a dive bar setting. I expected better value, especially considering the atmosphere. It wasn’t anything special drink-wise, just standard beers at a higher-than-expected price.

Overall, Burns Alley has potential with its unique vibe, but the attitude of the staff and the pricing really took away from the experience. I wanted to like it, but I left feeling like I wouldn’t go back.

googleReviews.author: Kyle
googleReviews.text: Stopped into Burns Alley Tavern with a friend after everything wrapped up for the day at a work event, and it ended up being one of the highlights of the trip. We were just out exploring late night and came across karaoke, which made it an easy decision to stay for a while. The vibe was laid back and fun, the crowd was into it, and it felt like a great spot to unwind after a long day. Drinks were reasonably priced, which was a nice bonus, and it was the kind of place you could hang out in without overthinking it. Definitely glad we found it and I’d come back again next time I’m in Charleston!

googleReviews.author: Tyler Yzaguirre
googleReviews.text: Make sure you go on a weekend for Claire! Out of my top 3 experiences for my first time in Charleston (coming from DC) both Claire and the bar tied for 3rd place. Make sure to be nice and patient with the bartenders, and they’ll take care of you. Don’t be a jerk if your sugar free Fru fru Red Bull isn’t super chilled.

googleReviews.author: J.C. Lochan
googleReviews.text: One the best bars near King Street for live music. The place is a huge College of Charleston hangout, and the staff there are pretty cool to interact with. The prices of drinks and food here are great as well, but there is a very limited selection of food. They will occasionally have food pop ups, though. They usually have great live music almost every night right on the stage by the bar. There are two "floors" to the place as well, with a good amount of seats each. Overall a great place to spend a couple of hours at.

The potato wedges and wings are fantastic. Brandy has my drink waiting for me at the bar.

Katie is by far the best day time bartender in Charleston. I mean this woman has a drink and shot ready when she sees me get out my car.

Amanda is new but man she is on point with her attention to everyone at the bar.

googleReviews.author: Pryncess Mad
googleReviews.text: Very nice place to shoot pool and grab a bite to eat! Music is good as well. Have fun every time I go there.

googleReviews.author: Thelma Washington
googleReviews.text: A friend of mine begged me to visit this place for years. When I got there I asked for a drink, and was disrespected, and I was completely ignored by both bartenders for over 40 minutes. Both bartenders became extremely rude and aggressive when I asked for a drink the second time. Both bartenders need to be fired or etiquette training is needed. This establishment will be a waste of your time.

googleReviews.text: Outstanding management, exceptional new drinks—especially the refreshing Cucumber Cilantro drink that even cilantro haters can enjoy—definitely coming back, and huge thanks to the amazing bartender Josette for her excellent recommendations!

googleReviews.author: Kiera Reynolds
googleReviews.text:
We tried going here last night for my friends bachelorette trip and it was the first bar we tried going to. There was no line and so we thought we could just walk right in but we got stopped by another person walking around and was talking with them. We were all of course alittle tipsy so we were standing by the doorway, but not totally blocking it. One bouncer was nice and was trying to tell us we needed to move aside but this other bouncer literally started yelling at us and making us feel so uncomfortable. I understand dealing with drunk people all night is probably not the most fun time but also this was our very first time downtown and our very first stop and we got treated so poorly . He was very rude and quite literally yelled at us multiple times and throwing his hands up at us
This made us, especially the bride very upset and was not a good start to what was supposed to be a very fun night.
I know we were in front of the doorway and not going around the rail they had set up but there no line and since it was our VERY first bar in Charleston, we were unsure
I just think you shouldn’t yell at a stranger the way that man yelled at a bunch a young girls who were just trying to celebrate. So 1 star because that bouncers rude attitude was our first impression on downtown and it was not a good one .

googleReviews.text: Drinks were great!! Thats all I had there! Nice vibe and it was karaoke night! Too much fun!!!

googleReviews.text: I’m not a frequent night life goer but I decided to go out tonight and I usually head here the night. Good music DJ good bartenders BUT I got stopped at the door…sign says no PLAIN WHITE TEES I had on a cream colored polo t-shirt with hint of grey specs. When I asked the doorman about it, it was clear that it was to his discretion on white he deemed what was considered “white” because I asked him if I could prove if it wasn’t white via the tag or description would he let me in and he said it’s what he perceived as white….thats crazy…I even showed the polo logo to show it wasn’t plain and get this…THE POLO LOGO IS IN WHITE and you can clearly see it’s not the same color as the shirt…I’m black with wicks by the way 🤷🏾‍♂️

googleReviews.author: Linda P.
googleReviews.text: We met up with some friends for lunch at Uptown Social while visiting Charleston in early March. We had their burger special with a beer and it was great. We almost couldn’t believe the price. Such a great deal! Food was fresh and serving size was perfect. Our server was friendly and helpful. I highly recommend this place.

googleReviews.author: Peter Welmerink
googleReviews.text: Had a new waiter apparently but he was friendly and was trying. Mis-ordered my drink...was a whiskey sour not a whiskey mule...but I like Buffalo Trace so...I drank it. Ordered Caesar Salad w/ chicken. That was good and tasty. Wife got a salad also and a beer. That was all good also. Atmosphere was great and no band on a Monday night so we could relax and talk. I WOULD recommend even if waiter seemed new... He was pleasant and he did come by the table plenty of times to make sure we were doing well. He did offer to comp but we said it was fine. It was.

googleReviews.author: Brownbiggy
googleReviews.text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
“Great vibe, but service needs backup!”

Uptown Social has a fun, high-energy atmosphere that makes it a solid choice if you’re looking to hang out and soak in the Charleston nightlife. The music was upbeat, the crowd was lively, and the space had that casual party vibe that’s perfect for a weekend out.

That said, service was really slow when we went—only one server seemed to be covering the whole floor, which definitely affected wait times. Didn’t try the drinks this time, but the menu looked good and reasonably priced for the area.

Still giving it 4 stars because the overall vibe and ambiance delivered. Just hope they have more staff next time—this place deserves smoother service to match its scene.

googleReviews.author: Bradford G
googleReviews.text: Uptown social is the perfect place to get social uptown. My wife and I are celebrated her promotion in Charleston and boy oh boy did we enjoy.. in nights out, uptown is the real McCoy . Greeted with sweet southern smiles, a blonde who goes by the name Katie took us old northern red cardinals under her all-knowing southern gull wing. I myself, an IPA indulger, asked for a recommendation(shhh I’m a novice drinker and that’s a good thing.), Katie was quick to offer recommendations for both me and my lady. We ordered one strawberry fields and a tropicalia. The Beatles were right when they sang strawberry fields forevvvverrr, because I could sip on that forever! Divine. Next we munched on the pretzel bites and Mac and cheese bites. And for our main, we did the hot honey pizza that our waitress recommended. Delicious and delightful. No crumbs left. A sweet spicy kick, but not overpowering. Pinch me, I think I was genuinely *in heaven*. Next time we find ourself in the historic city of Charleston we will be back for delicious drinks, darling service, and delightful bites!

googleReviews.author: ECHO-62
googleReviews.text:
Drinks are priced as expected for this area, however, if you dance and stand away from frim your drink, the barback would swoop in and grab your drink, even if its only half drunk.

Happened to me 3 times in one night, and the "door manager" offered to give me a free drink?!?!.

I was done with the night and tried to talk to the "door manager" and when i suggested that their barbacks make rational decisions about the drinks they pick up, it got nowhere. When i tried to suggest they try and teach the employees to better pick EMPTY cups instead of half empty cups, the local cops at the door told me to leave.

They know what they're doing and they wont correct this action, making people buy more drinks.

googleReviews.author: Tom
googleReviews.text:
This place is just amazing. Where to start? The history of the restaurant/building is amazing. The decor is just very retro, quirky and cool. There are a couple of levels inside and a couple of levels of rooftop seating. It really is fun.

We arrived right after they opened so it wasn’t particularly crowded. I have to return when there is live music and the place is hoping.

We sat at the bar and had a few drinks. Our bartender was friendly and knowledgeable. Henry’s has a great location. And looking forward to returning.

googleReviews.author: Anna Sophia
googleReviews.text:
The Tito's and lemonade serving size seemed smaller than usual. I ordered a chopped salad with added local shrimp and swapped Mediterranean vinaigrette for Caesar dressing. The shrimp was cooked perfectly, I asked for grilled. Service was good at the bar with the bartender being very polite and attentive. The cleanliness of the restroom was good but it did look a bit outdated with graffiti on the stall door. A credit card fee was charged. I felt the lunch was a little on the expensive side.
They offer live music in the evening . It was too hot & muggy for me to check out the rooftop bar.

googleReviews.author: ShubhalokG
googleReviews.text:
Got into Charlestown late and grabbed a late night meal and music at Henrys.  Sage gave an awesome overview of the menu and strongly suggested the shrimp and grits.  I was highly hesitant as I had Thomas Keller Bouchon shrimp  and grits and nothing ever was better...... well I was completely blown away by the Charleston Tasso gravy.  The definition on menu doesnt do it justice.  I learned that Tasso ham is made from smoked and spiced pork shoulder and has a delicious ending cayenne kick! Amazing intense flavor. The collards were a bangin sidekick again with an extra special hot flash kick flavor.

Sage is an excellent server with lots of information on Charleston.  If your in the industry, ask her about future passions in Pharma and Robotics.

Finally, Henrys is a great place for dancing to Sax and backbeat on huge floor.  Stevie Wonder "In the City" cover killed.  Chk it.

googleReviews.author: jose ignacio ortiz guerrero
googleReviews.text:
The place is very nice, good ambience, great decorations and furniture.
They have live music that is a great addition to the experience, the waiters are kind.
The food is nice, it tastes good but is a little overpriced (as almost everything on Charleston) but even so is a nice place.

googleReviews.author: Joe Rubino
googleReviews.text: Great spot right off the market. Has indoor and rooftop seating. We set at the bar and ordered a salad a triple slider special. The portions were huge. The sliders were pretty much regular size burger, Nashville chicken and crab cake. Great place to watch sports. The service is great and the place had a great vibe.

googleReviews.text: Karaoke Tuesday night. Mixed crowd of people, good sound system, online song requests and queueing. The host was fun and made sure everyone was welcome/invited to sing. Many people were using vape/ e-cigarettes indoors.

googleReviews.author: Alissa Curtis
googleReviews.text: Went here for a sunday night drag show with some friends and also alot of our first drag show experience! We had a great time and all the ladies were great and very crowd involved especially for the couple of Bachelorette and birthday party groups they had. It was a very entertaining and funny show and the drinks although kinda limited as far as selection were great as well! The bartenders that night were super friendly and very quick even while busy. Well deff be back again!

googleReviews.author: Justin Nichols
googleReviews.text:
Dudley’s is truly a gem and an essential part of Charleston’s nightlife. As the only gay bar in Charleston, Dudley’s provides a welcoming, inclusive, and safe space where everyone can be unapologetically themselves. The atmosphere is always warm, energetic, and full of community spirit.

Broke Collins deserves special recognition for bringing incredible entertainment and heart to the space. The performances are fun, bold, and full of personality, and they consistently create nights that are memorable and uplifting. You can feel the passion and effort that goes into every event.

Dudley’s isn’t just a bar—it’s a community hub, a place of celebration, and a reminder of how important queer spaces are, especially in the South. Grateful to have a place like this in Charleston that continues to show up, stand proud, and bring people together.

googleReviews.author: kris gonzalez

googleReviews.author: Jeffrey Hyde
googleReviews.text: I admit that I’m probably biased on this place because it is one of the places where my now wife and I went on our first date. However, I’ve been back several times since and it’s always the same… lots of groups hanging out taking turns singing. Their Hurricane is one of my favorites in NOLA because it’s sweeter than most others. They could stand to update their video system and probably lots of other things but it’s just a dive bar with karaoke. If you go in with that expectation, you’ll be more than pleased!!

googleReviews.author: Cody Smith
googleReviews.text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Review — The Cat’s Meow, New Orleans

Walking up to The Cat’s Meow on Bourbon Street already feels like stepping into a movie — but what
really made it special was the beautiful, kind-hearted girl at the door. My husband and I didn’t have our IDs on us at the moment, and instead of treating us badly, she was genuinely sweet, respectful, and human about it. That meant more than she probably realized.

We’re both Aquarians, so we definitely believe in good energy, good vibes, and good people — and she had all three. She made us feel welcome even when the answer had to be “not right now,” and that kind of kindness is rare on Bourbon Street.

I’ve heard about this place forever, and now I know why people love it. It’s not just the karaoke and the wild fun — it’s the people who work there. And honestly… I still need to come back for some Cat’s Meow “cat ears” and a night of singing my heart out.

Thank you for being kind when it mattered. We’ll be back. 🐱🎤

---

If you want, I can also make a short Google review version or a more playful, Bourbon-Street vibe version 😺

googleReviews.author: Dan Andsome Handsome
googleReviews.text: This was the best place in New Orleans for our Mardi Gras celebration.  The drinks were perfect and the people were great.  I hold the man named Nick in high esteem. Make sure you show them respect and you will get it back 💯 fold!  I will be going back, hopefully in the summer, if not, for sure next year again for Mardi Gras!  The karaoke kicks ass.  The MCs are always hyped up and get the crowd going.

googleReviews.author: Sean Z
googleReviews.text:
The Dungeon has the tourist formula down pretty well. It’s not trying to be fancy, and that works in its favor. The bartenders were friendly and quick with service, which kept things moving even when it got busy.

The place is laid out across several small rooms, including a dance floor on the upper level, which makes it fun to explore a bit rather than feeling like one big crowded space.

Their specialty frozen/slushy drink is worth trying. I recommend asking for it with the liqueur  they have the cherries soaking in, which adds a nice touch.

One thing that stood out was the strict no photos or video policy inside the venue. Honestly, that’s kind of refreshing. It cuts down on people constantly stopping in just to take selfies for social media and helps keep the vibe focused on actually enjoying the bar.

Overall, it’s a fun stop if you’re bar hopping in the Quarter and want something a little different.

googleReviews.author: Amy
googleReviews.text: We didn’t get food or drinks here. We mostly wanted to just check it out as it had good reviews. If you’re into goth, creepy, kinda satanic vibe, you might enjoy this place. Too bizarre for me, but the couple we were with loved it. Very dark inside, very loud music, friendly staff.

googleReviews.author: Punk-Nater
googleReviews.text:
Went in with expectations, left with secondhand embarrassment.

The place was nearly empty and somehow still managed to have a bad vibe.

The bartender—an older woman with grey hair and glasses—was aggressively rude from the jump. Yelling like banchee-witch! At one point, she literally screeched over the music to yell at a couple near us for taking selfies. Not photos of the bar—selfies against a blank wall in the back.

Yes, no photos of the establishment, got it. But the couple immediately apologized… multiple times. Instead of letting it go, she kept shaking her head, saying they “knew better,” and then yelled continuously. Thr male staff politely said as a reminder no pictures.  That was perfect.

It turned a simple misunderstanding into full-blown unnecessary drama and made the whole area uncomfortable.

So, lesson learned: don’t take your phone out at all unless you want to be publicly scolded.

The décor leaned heavily into an edgy (just for the sake of being edgy) asian bondage-style nude art that felt more awkward than provocative. (Especially given I am of Asian decent)

The music was loud emo/screamo that didn’t match the tiny, low-energy crowd.
On the plus side (or minus, depending on legality), the drinks were very strong. Like… questionably strong.

Overall: small crowd, weird energy, hostile service. If you’re into being yelled at for existing and awkward “shock value” aesthetics, this might be your place. Otherwise, I’d skip it.

googleReviews.text: Honestly this was my first time to the Dungeon and I truly love it. The music was on fire yes it is Metal but who doesn’t love Metal right. The Atmosphere is the greatest service you could’ve asked for the best especially of Mardi Gras huge shout out to the amazing LADY’s that took amazing care of everyone at the bar all day long the on with the Devil looking masking in her hair and the other with the Pom Pom in her hair thank you ladies I can in late you all were amazing much love.

googleReviews.author: Malia Connor
googleReviews.text: We decided on this bar as the last drink for our visit. The server suggested the fleur de lis, a great switch up since I was only sipping on espresso martinis this week. We opted to not sit at bar since I have motion sickness but the window spot we chose near jazz band was perfect.

googleReviews.author: Danielle M.
googleReviews.text:
Such a great experience at the Carousel Bar & Lounge!

This is the perfect hangout spot for professionals or anyone looking to unwind in a classy, laid-back setting. The ambience was chill and inviting, with a live band that set the perfect tone for the night. The atmosphere overall was lively but still comfortable you could relax, enjoy good conversation, and soak in the energy of New Orleans.

Of course, the highlight is the carousel bar itself it slowly spins as you sip your drink, which was such a fun and unique experience! The vibe here is truly unmatched. Whether you’re a local or just visiting, this spot is an absolute must when in New Orleans.

googleReviews.author: Daniella Crowder
googleReviews.text:
The Carousel Bar was such a fun experience during our trip to New Orleans. Sitting at the rotating carousel bar while enjoying a drink is definitely something unique you don’t get just anywhere.

There are only about 12 seats at the actual carousel, so if you’re hoping to sit there you may have to stand nearby and wait for someone to get up. There are other places to sit in the bar, but the real experience is sitting at the carousel while it slowly rotates.

I was lucky enough that a very kind lady offered her seat to me and my son, which made the experience even more special.

I ordered the French 007 and it was absolutely delicious. Definitely worth stopping in for a drink if you’re in New Orleans.

⭐ Highly recommend for the atmosphere and the experience.

googleReviews.author: Christian H
googleReviews.text:
Iconic bar!

Really worth it go for the main attraction, getting on the carousel. It takes about 15 minutes to do a full rotation, but it's first come first serve and can be quite busy/hard to get on it depending on the time/day. The vieux carré is there signature cocktail and would recommend.

googleReviews.author: August Rudisell
googleReviews.text: Such a dope place. It’s the set of one of my favorite movies. Drinks are immaculate - a much better place for drinks than Bourban St. plus it has a spinning bar!

googleReviews.author: Jane Johnson
googleReviews.text: Thought it was going to be a shady experience but was pleasantly surprised by the show. Absolutely hilarious show. Drinks were great. Inside the club was artistically done, very fun. Staff was welcoming and pleasant. I will definitely go back for another show. Just risky enough to be called a burlesque show but not trashy. All the girls made me and my friends laugh.

googleReviews.author: Екатерина Андреева
googleReviews.text:
Wow — what an outstanding show!
New Orleans High Society completely exceeded my expectations.

An important note for anyone wondering about the repertoire and vibe: as Miss Angie Z herself says, burlesque performers are strippers and they love (and appreciate) money — so active tipping during the show is very welcome, though never mandatory.

The strip element is absolutely there — bright, bold, and playful — but this is so much more than a simple striptease.
Live jazz, incredible singing, a rich atmosphere, fantastic burlesque performances, and so much humor. Truly laugh-out-loud moments.

One small practical note: don’t expect fancy cocktails — the bar is simple with straightforward drinks, which honestly fit the vibe just fine.

I loved this show far more than I expected to and I’m genuinely so happy I went.
Fun, sexy, funny, and full of life — highly recommended.

googleReviews.author: Maddison Taitano
googleReviews.text: Took my girls to the allways lounge in night 2 of our Bachelorette trip. We saw the Diamonds Burlesque show and wow, wow, wow!!!!!! It was so much fun, very interactive and the show went on a bit longer than expected (a good thing!). It had open seating, which was nice, and the acts were incredible! Tickets and drinks were well priced for the event as well.

googleReviews.author: Walter Weeks
googleReviews.text: I’ll tell you this much, greetings from queer mountain is now one of my favorite experiences by far! Omg everyone slayed!! How does that happen that every single act slays?! I really cant wait to go back. Besides being extremely talented they were all such sweet human beings. It was truly one of those experiences where a person thanks the universe and really means it so thank you to all the acts and the universe for making them a brilliant display of humanity🥰🥰🥰🥰

googleReviews.author: Ryan Nguyen
googleReviews.text: My friends and I bar hopped here from Ohm Lounge in the Warehouse District. The vibe was definitely hype when we arrived! They were actually playing some popular Spanish pop hits. I really liked outside patio since it added a lot more space where you can chill from the crowd. Service was really slow. My friend and I tried to ask for water for our group but it took so long for them to respond. Eventually, we were able to get the waters. Although, it really was a busy night so I guess I’ll give them the benefit of the doubt. Overall, a pretty fun bar with fun vibes.

googleReviews.author: Maybank Media 7
googleReviews.text:
Razzoo is always a vibe and one of the best bands on Bourbon St. I feel safe walking in and have never had any tension inside. The staff is attentive and the food and drinks aren’t overpriced.

We happened to go on a football Sunday vs the Falcons. Being from ATL, all of our fam was there. It was a vibe to say the least.

googleReviews.author: Alyssa Curtis
googleReviews.text:
Stopped in on a Tuesday night not expecting much and ended up having one of those “why don’t we do this more often?” evenings. The place had a small but lively crowd, just enough people to feel energized without being packed, and the band absolutely made the night. You could tell they were having as much fun as the audience, and that energy was contagious. Great mix of songs, solid sound, and the kind of vibe where you find yourself tapping your foot without realizing it.
The atmosphere felt welcoming and easygoing, perfect for hanging out, listening to good music, and enjoying the night without any fuss. It didn’t feel rushed or overly loud, just a great spot to unwind. The drinks were well made and tasted great, but they can add up quickly if you’re not paying attention. Still, for the overall experience, it felt worth it.
If you’re looking for a laid-back place with live music, good drinks, and a fun crowd, this is a solid choice. Definitely a spot I’d come back to, especially on a night when there’s a band playing.

googleReviews.text: Good deal on drinks and a clearly marked menu. Great bands playing 70's 80's on up. The Phunky Monkeys are great! Staff are friendly!

googleReviews.text: Overall I rate this 4 stars but with that being said it was some of the best entertainment on the street tonight. The bar didn’t know how to make some simple shots, but what they didn’t know was made up for with the amazing band that was playing. We sat for about 30 minutes enjoying the songs. Singing and having a good time.

googleReviews.text: Mother's lounge is the best new dance bar! Everyone is welcome there. They have bingo nights and drag nites and karaoke nights! googleReviews.text: Amazing bar! Great vibe! Awesome drinks! Great bar food!!  Trent and Montana are the best!!!!! Love you guys! Best Bingo!!!!!

googleReviews.author: Chistine
googleReviews.text: We had my daughter’s pre wedding party at Mother’s Lounge. The service was great. They accommodated all of our needs for a 4 hour private time. Drinks and food were excellent. Staff were friendly and courteous. We would definitely recommend this venue .

googleReviews.author: Max Cervantes
googleReviews.text: Clean, stylish, colorful. The rainbow hallway is photoshoot worthy, the disco ball and mirrored walls echo a 70’s vibe while the music and projector screen bring you right into the moment. Montana was incredibly friendly behind the bar and made this centrally located downtown bar extremely inviting. A unexpected gem for a visitor.

googleReviews.author: Ethan Boudreaux
googleReviews.text:
Best bar in Baton Rouge, hands down!
Mother’s Lounge is more than just a bar — it’s a whole experience. The cocktails are creative, strong, and beautifully crafted (seriously, you won’t find a better espresso martini in town). Mother’s strikes the perfect balance between classy and comfortable, with cozy lighting, great music, and an effortlessly inclusive vibe.

The staff and ownership are the heart of the place — Montanna and Trent go above and beyond to make everyone feel welcome and seen. Whether you’re flying solo or rolling deep with friends, you’ll feel like part of the family by your second drink.

And then there’s the drag. Phenomenal. The queens bring it every single time — fun, fierce, and full of talent. It’s one of the few spots in the city where the LGBTQ+ community and allies can come together and truly let loose.

Come for the drinks, stay for the drag, and leave with a new favorite bar. 💅🔥

googleReviews.author: Jeimuzu Sama
googleReviews.text:
I visited this karaoke bar last night hoping for a fun night out, but unfortunately, the atmosphere felt very unwelcoming. I noticed that after signing up to sing, I was skipped, even though only two people were ahead of me. When I asked, I was told “everyone’s getting skipped,” but it didn’t seem like that was true for everyone…mainly those who didn’t look like the regulars.

There was a woman performing, and suddenly her music distorted mid-song, which felt suspicious. Overall, the environment didn’t feel inclusive, and it seemed like certain guests weren’t given the same chance to enjoy the experience.

If you’re looking for a karaoke spot where everyone gets a fair shot to sing and feel welcomed, I’d recommend thinking twice before coming here.

googleReviews.author: Trisha Hartzog
googleReviews.text: I was there with a whole party, and we all got kicked out because me and another person had to escort one of our drunk friends out. No one else was super drunk, me and the other person escorting her were completely sober. There was no disturbance to any guests, the bartenders, or any other staff members. The bouncer was also talking so disrespectfully about her as we were leaving. If y'all can't handle drunk people *already leaving the bar* then y'all shouldn't be running a bar. I wouldn't recommend going, especially in a large group or if you care about your friends' safety.

googleReviews.author: Kimberly Santangelo
googleReviews.text: We held my daughters gender reveal in the large  private bar room area on Nov 20th.  We got a great deal on it for the afternoon from the manager.  The room was perfect!  It was not only decorated for the season but it was so very neat & clean.  The new parents to be used the stage area for the big moment & there were plenty chairs/tables for everyone.  All employees were accommodating and professional.   Times are hard, so we are beyond grateful that they gave us a spectacular deal on use of this space.  Family & friends for both mom & dad to be were able to find out at the same time that ITS A BOY!!

googleReviews.author: Daniel Scheer
googleReviews.text: I'm giving The Station Bar and Grill five stars because they do exactly what they are supposed to do. We had an excellent selection of draft beer to choose from including the local favorites. Although no frozen drinks were available, the mixed drinks were correctly made and tasted great. We got there for $6 burgers and free comedy on a Wednesday and were slightly dismayed to find a headliner with a $15 entry... but that ended up being well worth it. The $6 burgers were phenomenal and would be at their regular price too. Can't wait to go back again, but think I'll wait for the next headline show, because that put the whole experience over the top. One last note... they call themselves a bar and grill, but I would clarify that they are more bar than grill. Orders are taken and served at the bar... but don't let that keep you away!

googleReviews.author: Ian Haneline
googleReviews.text:
I didn't know what to expect of this place, but it was a lot of fun. My buddy rented out a room for his 40th birthday party and had a karaoke DJ.
Bartenders were attentive and the drinks good. Everyone was friendly and I'll likely go back again.

googleReviews.author: Carrie Broussard
googleReviews.text: The restaurant was cool even though we didn't necessarily find what we were looking for. It still turned out to be a decent experience. What really made me reconsider the star numbers was the cook/chef. He made a grilled cheese sandwich for me even though it's not on the menu because I don't eat meat. I really loved the flexibility and consideration given to me, the customer.

googleReviews.author: Michele Hutchins
googleReviews.text: The Red Stick Social exceeded all of my expectations. The space and building were simply amazing. The staff (specifically Angel Beadle) made creating a very special wedding reception so smooth since I was OUT OF STATE! They took care of every detail to help the night become one of the best celebrations we have had. They listened and took action on each request for seating, food, and entertainment. I heard rave reviews from my guests which put me at ease. The food was delicious! We had food for the rehearsal dinner as well as the reception. All different items and all were enjoyed! If you are in need of a special & unique place in Baton Rouge for any type of an event, I would highly recommend Red Stick Social. We also enjoyed the brunch on Sunday that was open to the public. Once again, the food was delicious.

googleReviews.author: Jamie Anderson
googleReviews.text: drinks are almost $16 (gratuity included). you would think with prices like this red stick would have experienced bartenders. i simply asked for a RUM PUNCH. the bartender Danny googled the ingredients in my face and still made the drink INcorrectly. besides the drink tasting disgusting he did not originally even put the grenadine in the drink. he handed me the drink and i asked what it was because a rum punch is a red/orange color. the drink was strictly orange he replied rudely “a rum punch” i said “well can you add the grenadine?” and he looked confused but added it still. he also was NOT garnishing the drinks at all if i’m paying $16 for a drink i want everything that comes with the drink. orange, cherry whatever it doesn’t matter at the prices of items at red stick the bartenders should be experienced OR properly trained. Later a friend offered to buy me a drink and of course we ended up getting Danny as our bartender again. I ordered a tequila sunrise and again, it was NOT make correctly and the drinks were NOT garnished. in total we ordered 3 drinks at that moment my tequila sunrise, a long island and a amaretto sour not ONE drink was garnished with any type of fruit . however, shout out to the bartender ANGELINA for remaking me drink correctly and it tasted amazing. If you go here definitely look for her she’s so sweet and her drinks were great!

googleReviews.author: Jason Lambert
googleReviews.text: Went there to bowl, called ahead, was told there was no wait. Got there at 8pm and was told we couldn't get a lane, they weren't renting anymore lanes due to "mechanical issues". Very cool environment tho. Mind you it's January and 30° outside so we didn't explore outside.

googleReviews.author: Derrick Foster
googleReviews.text:
Awesome environment.
Went there for Skip Bentons 5th year anniversary for his law practice and had a great time.
I did not ask who catered the food for the event that I attended but if it was catered by Red Stick Social, they did a phenomenal job.
We were in a private room on the 5th floor of the building which has a four lane bowling alley, rooftop access and a very large area which is perfect for any type of large gathering, birthday party etc.
Did not know that this place existed in downtown Baton Rouge.

googleReviews.author: Joe Vice
googleReviews.text:
NEVER thought I would do this. I have been a patron of this place for almost 20 years(use to live in an apartment during college right down the street). I don't come in as much anymore as I live on the other side of Birmingham now, but I have come by a few times, maybe 4 in the past 2 or 3 years. I love singing kareoke, I keep to myself as I am 48 years old and just like to relax, especially after work. Last night, I came in, had been there a few weeks ago and sang kareoke and nothing out of the ordinary, and I was told "You creeped people out have to leave and hang out somewhere else". I have a good idea what the real issue is and that is a completely FALSE rumor going around about me. For almost 20 years, I have NEVER caused a scene or been told to leave till last night.

If I werent being honest, I wouldn't be this open about it. False rumor created more than likely, by my ex and her "Bar friends", has spilled over to several places i use to sing kareoke at. Just absolutely amazing that I have such fond memories of this place for nearly two decades and I was told and treated like I was last night when, again, ive never caused a problem here.

He doesn’t know Me And I don’t know him. So why else would he refuse to acknowledge me in the least bit. Not even a hello

googleReviews.text: Had a great time. Last time in this place was 25 yrs ago. Wow memories, good memories. All new folks of course. Still friendly , great service good atmosphere . Be going back. No food .

googleReviews.author: Ryan Rylander
googleReviews.text: Stopped in while I was in town on business. I know from experience, you can't judge a book by its cover. And Bourbon Street Bar was just what I needed. First thing I noticed was the clean parking lot. Signs posted warned of possible physical violence for those who dispose their butts on the ground. Walking up, I recognized the architecture as a forgotten relic from yesterdoodle. It's an old Pizza Hut, dressed up with plywood and awnings. I knew I was in the right place, when I opened the door, and was greeted by a couple of puppers and the bartender. This was 10 months ago, so her name escapes me. But I have a pretty good feeling she's still there, shining glasses and crafting cocktails. I wanted a quaint place to hang out. And found just that. A couple locals, a couple well behaved pups, the bartender, and the elderly owner rounded out the roster of everyone in attendance. The owner had to be in his mid 80s, and was sharp as ever! With a golden sense of humor to match! I had a great time with my boss and a coworker. We were in town to purchase a machine built locally to Birmingham. We work back in Wisconsin. After a couple drinks, and a few rounds of fetch, I felt like I was with old friends. We talked about the area, things to do, things to see. Interesting history and happenings. I didn't want to leave! But, the hotel wasn't cheap, so we went back there to get our money's worth!! We definitely got our money's worth here!! Bourbon Street Bar and Lounge is a 10/10!! 5 stars! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Would recommend!!

googleReviews.author: Tod Kimbro
googleReviews.text: This place is charmingly divey, and I can see why it’s a neighborhood fave, but I had a bad experience. Waited at the bar for the barmaid to finish her break. I had been standing there for nearly five minutes when 3 ladies walked in. The barmaid had been standing in the corner, talking to a fellow employee. When she approached the bar, she decided to serve the ladies first. Honest mistake? Maybe. But the  ladies had a complicated drink order and I only wanted a canned beer. Had she noticed me, she could have taken my order, realized how simple it was and cracked the beer. Only that didn’t happen. She went in the back room and took about 8 minutes to make an a time-consuming bucket-style drink for the ladies. When she finally took my drink order, she got it wrong twice. I get it: “Jai Alai” sounds a lot like “High Life” lol. She handed me a bottle of High Life. When I clarified that I wanted the “Jai Alai IPA,” she said “Oh, the IPA.” She then handed me a can that said “IPA” but was not the beer I had ordered. She had already cracked it, and by now I had given up, so I drank it. And it was a pretty terrible beer. I had planned to drink a few beers, because I had about 15 minutes to kill before picking up a food order. But I spent about 13 waiting for service and then had to chug something disgusting so my food wouldn’t be cold. Barmaid seemed very nice, and I don’t think she meant to inconvenience me. But this was really bad service and should be noted

googleReviews.text: This restaurant popped up on my tiktok so I asked my mom if she wanted to try it w|me. We ended up going to order in store. The food though was great! We will definitely be ordering again.

googleReviews.author: Gina Castiron
googleReviews.text:
I’ve been a loyal regular at Gabes for a long time, and honestly, that’s why this is so frustrating to even say. I love the atmosphere, the bartenders, the staff, and the overall vibe. A lot of the workers know me by name, and I know them too. Some even have my personal number because I’m there that often. Johnny is one of my favorites, and the staff is a huge reason I continue to come back.

And to be clear Gabes itself is NOT the issue. I will absolutely continue to support the business because the bartenders, workers, drinks, deals, and overall environment are amazing. My frustration is specifically with the way karaoke is being run by the DJ.

At this point, the rotation system feels completely inconsistent and honestly unfair. We’re constantly told there’s a “rotation,” but it really doesn’t seem like there actually is one. You can sign up early, wait for hours, ask where you are in line, and still somehow get skipped while the same people sing two or three times before you even get called again once.

That’s the issue.

It’s not about who sings the best, who’s friends with who, or who deserves more stage time. It’s about professionalism and consistency. If you tell customers there’s a rotation, then there needs to actually BE a rotation that’s followed fairly. A visible sign-up list or queue would solve so much confusion because right now people are sitting there for 3+ hours waiting, eventually leaving out of frustration, and then suddenly getting called after they walk out the door.

That’s disheartening, especially when you’ve spent your entire night there supporting the business, buying drinks, tipping bartenders, and contributing to the atmosphere.

I’m not trying to be rude or difficult, but common sense and fairness matter. If you’re running karaoke professionally, there needs to be structure and accountability. Otherwise it just feels random and frustrating for the people who genuinely support the place week after week.

Again, I love Gabes and will continue to support Gabes. This post is not directed at the business itself. It’s directed at the way karaoke is currently being managed, because it could and should be handled much better.

googleReviews.author: Like A Sir
googleReviews.text:
In a city of highly stressful jobs and a generally stressful outlook on life post-theeventthatshallnotbenamed, there are alot of bars that offer alot of different things. Having been in the area over half a decade, I've been to most. That knowledge in mind, I can just about guarantee that no matter how many places you visit, you'd struggle to find a place that is genuinely as good of a time as Moody's.

It's a special kind of place where you really would have to visit to understand, but once you understand, it's the kind of place you'll want to visit often. The bar tending team at the place is awesome at making sure you don't wait too long to enjoy a libation, and I've heard great things about the food that I've yet to partake in. The gals are gorgeous, the people there err towards friendly, and you couldn't pick a better spot to enjoy yourself without all of the BS that oft comes with going out in the area.

Just don't come in and be the BS yourself, or you will find yourself outside by yourself.

googleReviews.author: Nate B
googleReviews.text: I really enjoyed this place. Music was good on Tuesday night. Beer was good. Nice location. I would definitely recommend this place.

googleReviews.author: Kathryn Jones (Katie)
googleReviews.text: Great place to go for locals and out-of-towners alike. Can get very noisy and packed quite easily. This can be hard on the bartenders so always remember to give them grace and be understanding. Yes, the place is dark, dirty, and has a certain unpleasant smell. But it’s a dive- it is what it is. Not everyone’s cup of tea, but a lot of folks really love and find enjoyment here. They do serve some pretty yummy bar food which was a nice surprise. Love their phiddle fries and they have really good wings as well. For anyone who wants to know more about the wing flavors- Jacob told me that the Voodoo flavor is very hot and the Zombie flavor is sweet with a little spiciness.

googleReviews.author: Chris Robertson
googleReviews.text:
I've only been to Voodoo twice since I moved to Huntsville and the second time was significantly better! Probably helps that I went for karaoke on a Monday night, instead of being packed in there shoulder-to-shoulder late on a Saturday.
Super-cool spot, just a tad claustrophobic, if that kinda thing bothers you.

googleReviews.author: Judson Rogers
googleReviews.text: Voodoo Lounge Bar & Grill has a great basement vibe with solid drinks that won’t break the bank. The atmosphere strikes a nice balance between lively and relaxed, and the band brought some serious energy. Definitely a spot worth checking out.

googleReviews.text: First time visiting on 3/15. We went for drinks, but were told they didn't have a drink menu. However, the bartender concocted drinks for us. I decided to order wings and fries. The portion was excellent for the price. The fries were crispy, but the wings were super rubbery. The sauce also did not stick to the wings well at all. The atmosphere was super chill — not many people on the inside at the time we were there which was around 6ish. However, the outside was a little more lively. The server was super friendly and overall it was a good, chill vibe.

googleReviews.author: Johnny Wagnon
googleReviews.text:
Saw Afroman here the other day. Everything was okay but there was a handful of things that wasn't.

I wish security was better or more observant. Someone grabbed a guy beside me by the throat and it was up to the crowd to stop him, no security ever showed up or kicked that guy out.

All of the people around me was filthy drunk and falling over that was probably the most unenjoyable part. I know it's nothing the bar can control specifically but maybe there should be some better limits so the people that are stumbling and can't even stand can't get more alcohol.

I also reached out via Facebook when this event was announced to see if I was supposed to buy tickets or if you just show up (because I've not been there before) and I never heard back but thankfully I saw they shared a low ticket warning on a event page that I wasnt aware of.

Im not sure if it was a timing thing or if Afroman was really late but it was posted he would be on stage at 9 but he wasn't out until 10:30 and only played til 11:20. I enjoyed getting to hear songs that I love but it felt so short. Again it might not be the bars fault on that one but I wanted to mention it.

googleReviews.author: Colin Duckworth
googleReviews.text:
I've been to the Coppertop sporadically in the past, but recently I've been meeting up with friends and coworkers here every Thursday afternoon. This place delivers exactly what we're looking for.

The food is a huge plus for us. For a small bar, they're running an exceptional kitchen. From standbys like a Philly cheese steak or hot wings (always ask for extra crispy 😉), to the daily special, which can be anything from meatloaf and green bean casserole to Hawaiian pulled pork sliders topped with a fried pickle, Coppertop's kitchen shines every time I order... and always comes in under $10 including tax.

The service is spot on from my perspective. I'm always here on the same day and before they get too busy, so can't speak for the entire staff or the night scene, but Aaron consistently ensures my friends have a great experience, with just the right amount of attention. If a friend walks in late, Aaron has a chilled glass in his hand before he's figured out where he's going to sit down.

I'm stoked to have this business in my neighborhood.

googleReviews.author: Kathryn Jones (Katie)
googleReviews.text: Indoor and outdoor seating. Smoking is allowed in the bar area- separate rooms with dart boards and pool tables. Really enjoyed their hot wings. Garlic cheese curds and tots are also good. Lester is a great bartender and very attentive.

googleReviews.author: Tabitha Draper
googleReviews.text:
Had a great time here on a Saturday for a collection of bands. The place is larger than. It seemed from the outside.  The stage area was small, and the sound system design/setup could use some improvement. It had 2 large rooms for gaming and billiards, so I think that may be their main draw.
We had fried pickles, and they were great. Drinks were affordable and made well. Friendly staff, nice sized crowd for the venue. Seating was limited to some booths on the wall and the bar  when the bands were playing because they had to move the tables to make space. We didn't mi d standing, and you could go out to the patio and sit also.

Smoking is allowed, which was great for us, but it was not smoky inside and I think alot of people still went outside to smoke.

We will definitely be back!

googleReviews.author: David Kerr
googleReviews.text:
I knew I didn’t want to cook tonight, so I jumped on Resy to see what might have an open reservation. That’s how we ended up at a place I’d somehow never heard of.

And honestly, that’s usually a good sign.

Enter The Walk-In.

The place has this interesting mix going on. It feels Southern when you walk in - relaxed, comfortable, a little quirky - but the food leans Asian in ways that make the menu fun to poke around.

So we what we usually do when we’re somewhere new. We ordered a handful of things and figured we’d sort it out when it hit the table.

The black garlic deviled eggs were the first thing out. Just two halves, but really interesting. Salty in a good way with soy sauce, bonito, green onions, and sesame. Familiar, but not something you see every day.

The crab rangoon was excellent. Crispy and hot with a mango sweet and sour sauce that worked really well.

The kung pao bao buns were great too. Crispy chicken, crushed peanuts, soft buns. Good stuff.

We also tried the bulgogi grilled cheese, which comes as four little pull-apart Hawaiian roll sliders with beef tenderloin, kimchi, and mozzarella. Sweet rolls, savory beef, a little tang from the kimchi. A fun combination.

And because I’m me, we added the burger too. Patty melt style with house chips. Cooked perfectly.

Somewhere in the middle of all that I realized I was eating tater tots with chopsticks. Which felt like a pretty good summary of the whole experience.

They’ve got a patio outside and a shelf full of board games. I spotted Sorry and that was the end of that.

And I’m proud to report I ended the night with a victory.

Super fun little place. Quiet. Quirky. The kind of spot you’re happy you stumble into.

Some nights you just get lucky.

Service was as always, exceptional.  Shelby and the other sweet girl were both amazing.  They helped make our dinner feel special and cared to us extremely well.  They even helped to several photos of the group in front of the Christmas tree.

We’ve had many great experiences here, but they made it one of the best.

googleReviews.author: Cassandra Trawick
googleReviews.text: My coworker and I visited this place while in town on business.  I love the concept.  It’s an old house, looks like an old plantation house, turned into a restaurant/bar.  When you drive up the front of the house has the big white columns and lots of windows.  It definitely looks like a place that used to own slaves.  I found a staircase while looking for the bathroom that was hidden and figured that was for the “help.”  The dining area is not very spacious, but it went along with the theme.  Our table was super close to the others around it, you had no choice but to get to know your neighbors.  I got a drink recommended by our server.  It was so good, but I can’t remember the name or her name.  We had just eaten, so we didn’t get food, but our neighbors seemed to be enjoying their food.  The service was amazing here.  Everyone was so gracious and kind.  Everyone was dressed professionally and seemed to enjoy themselves.  Our drinks came out super fast too.  I explored the space a bit to find a restroom.  That’s when I saw that little staircase.  The bathroom was cute and clean.  The house looked a bit like a museum.  I’d go back again to at least have a chance to try some food.

googleReviews.author: Blair Bauer
googleReviews.text:
We went here last night for a Saturday night girls’ night and had a party of 6. As soon as we walked up, we were impressed with the presentation, atmosphere, and the vibes of the library lounge and the hotel. We were seated immediately and our server was Taja! She was super personable and fun, and she did a great job. The drinks were all delicious and we enjoyed all of the drinks. Although, at about 9:30pm after only one of us had ordered an espresso martini and the bar said they couldn’t make anymore of them which seemed too early in the night for that. We ordered a few appetizers, the first of which was the pimento cheese “beignets” which were amazing!! We expected the rest of the food to follow suit. The charcuterie board was decent, the truffle fries were almost plain French fries with one or two cheese sprinkles on them, and we got the dessert sampler which was a huge disappointment. We ordered the crème brûlée, brownie, key like pie, and peach cobbler to be in the sampler and we got the brownie, red velvet cake, a cookie (?), and something that looked like white cake with green jelly icing on it (key lime pie?), and Taja said that the kitchen told her to essentially “take it or leave it”. One of the girls in the group recognized the cookie as being from Whole Foods, so I would not be surprised if everything came from a grocery store cookie, cupcake, or brownie.

All of that to say, I would still suggest you check out this cool spot, but I would not take a chance on any of the food except the pimento cheese “beignets”.

googleReviews.author: Megan Williams
googleReviews.text: Had an absolute blast- lucky to follow Miki's journey for many years! Her team is top notch! The ambiance is so inviting- you can tell Miki really poured her heart into this project. The food was fresh, tasty and fun, you really get an authentic street food experience! The karaoke was so user friendly and not intimidating, even for a novice like me! I highly recommend for a date night, family party, club get together- you will leave with a new favorite hang out spot!🎤🎤🎉💜

googleReviews.author: Tyranni Plunkett
googleReviews.text:
Dude this is the best spot to go for a good meal and affordable drinks before getting onto karaoke
I was so nervous to get up there but I will bring friends forever. It's the perfect spot. The atmosphere is so great and I will recommend this to every person who comes into my bar from now on!

googleReviews.author: Joe Cho
googleReviews.text: This restaurant is a karaoke restaurant with Korean food. The English description of the pajeon was "Seafood & vegetable pancake," but it was smaller than expected, and I could not find seafood in it. Not many chicken wings. They are spicy with a gochujang base. It was delicious, though. If you don't like spicy food, you can order the sauce separately. The ramen and cup bop were pretty standard. What makes this restaurant special is the feeling of having a fun party with strangers. I'm not a good singer. So I just clapped along to the songs people were singing. When the songs ended, many people cheered and seemed to be enjoying themselves. You can feel like a singer. Of course, I guess the food included the price of the song. You don't have to pay extra for singing. Have a good time with your friend at Miki's.

googleReviews.author: SHE. Event Indy - Non Profit CARMEL, In
googleReviews.text:
Title: Disappointing Experience Despite a Nice Atmosphere

My friend and I recently met in Louisville, Kentucky, to enjoy a karaoke night together after 49 years of friendship. We were excited to celebrate this special occasion at what seemed to be a great spot.
We chose karaoke 🎤 That’s our thing.
Unfortunately, our experience was marred by the management of the karaoke session. After patiently waiting for over an hour, we noticed that our songs continued to be pushed back, while many patrons were called up multiple times. When I approached the karaoke host to express my concerns, I was met with indifference and rudeness. Instead of receiving help, I was told that being nice might yield better results, which felt disrespectful given our patience.

Seeking assistance, I turned to the bartender, who unfortunately referred me back to the same unhelpful host. The lack of respect and attentiveness from the staff overshadowed our evening.

While the venue itself is aesthetically pleasing, the treatment we received left us feeling disrespected and unwelcome. I regret to say that I will not be returning to this karaoke spot. It’s a shame, as we came for a fun night and left feeling disappointed.

googleReviews.author: Niel Randall
googleReviews.text:
I recently visited Miki's Karaoke Bar, and it was an incredible experience! The food was top-notch--every dish was flavorful and perfectly prepared. From the appetizers to the desserts, everything was delicious and beautifully presented.  The Korean fried wings and the spicy pork stir fry was off the chain.

What truly sets Miki's apart is Miki herself. She is a wonderful person who goes above and beyond to make sure her guests feel welcome. Her friendly and genuine nature creates a great atmosphere, making everyone feel at home. Whether she's helping out with karaoke or chatting with customers, Miki's presence makes the night special.

Miki's Karaoke Bar offers a perfect blend of great food and a lively, enjoyable environment. If you're looking for a place to enjoy good food and fun times, I highly recommend Miki's.

googleReviews.author: Melissa Claridy
googleReviews.text:
Visiting Louisville for the first time and I always enjoy hitting a karaoke place to truly get a sense of the local flavor. I asked the house band that played at my corporate event where they would recommend, and ALL of them said to go to Akikos, hands down.

They were 1000000% correct that this place was AMAZING! We went on a Wednesday and arrived just as they were opening. And there were already about ten singers in queue! The KJ was super nice, and the bartender Trent was very accommodating, even once it started to get busy. Beers were pretty cheap, too.

I didn't realize the bars in Louisville closed and FOUR A.M. 🤯 which meant that I think I sang *at least* ten songs... It did get pretty busy at one point so the wait got a little long, but by then I was having too much fun to care.

Their music list didn't have some of the more obscure songs I do, but it definitely was extensive! Only suggestion would be to upgrade the website they use for guests to search for songs.

If I ever make it back to Louisville, I will definitely be hitting up Akikos again!!

googleReviews.author: Carys Brown
googleReviews.text: If you’re a woman please go with friends, and do not go to the back patio by yourself, there seemed to be a pack of men outside that were really rude once you established your not interested. Bartenders and staff were lovely and welcoming and it was so fun to sing karaoke, plus everyone is so supportive even if you suck at singing.

We were then aggressively approached (5 out of town women) by the male bartender about the tip. Super uncomfortable. Do not recommend.

googleReviews.text: This is a cute little bar with a front room playing music, then karaoke in the back room! It was awesome and I would absolutely return, the DJ was great and kind and the bartenders were very nice. They do not sell food.

googleReviews.text: Holy Moly did my team and I have the BEST time ever. We did not know what to expect and it did not disappoint. We had a phenomenal time, team building at its finest.
